Taekwondo : 80 pratiquants réussissent les épreuves de passage de grade
items.description: Lomé, 8 nov. (ATOP) – La Fédération togolaise de taekwondo (FTTKD) a organisé un examen de passage de grade, du Dan (ceinture) 1 au Dan 4, le dimanche 8 novembre à Lomé. Au total, 80 candidats ont réussi les différentes épreuves, en attendant la proclamation officielle des résultats prévue dans deux semaines. Une trentaine de clubs ont pris part à cette évaluation qui a enregistré une centaine de candidats, dont une vingtaine de filles et de femmes. Parmi eux, 54 aspirent au Dan 1, 16 au Dan 2, 16 au Dan 3 et 14 au Dan 4. L’examen vise à améliorer les mouvements et le niveau technique des pratiquants. Les candidats ont compéti dans plusieurs disciplines, notamment le Kibon (mouvements de base), le Poumsea (formes de défense et d’attaque), le Hoshinsul (défense contre les saisies), les techniques d’attaque et de défense, le Kyukpa (casse), les coups de pied, le Kyurigi (combats) et la théorie portant sur les noms des mouvements. Les postulants au Dan 4 ont également présenté, la veille, une soutenance de dix minutes sur un thème de leur choix. Les candidats de moins de 16 ans ont été soumis aux épreuves du Poom, tandis que ceux âgés de 17 ans et plus ont concouru pour les grades supérieurs. Au Kyurigi, les postulants au Dan 1 se sont affrontés entre eux et avec un candidat. Ceux du Dan 2 ont combattu entre eux et contre deux athlètes de ceinture rouge. Pour les Dan 3 et 4, les combats ont également opposé les candidats à trois ceintures noires. A l’épreuve de casse, les moins de 16 ans ont brisé une planche en bois, contre deux planches pour les candidats aux Dan 2, 3 et 4. Le président de la FTTKD, Boyodi Hénoc, s’est réjoui de la tenue de cet examen, après deux années sans organisation de passage de grade. Il a expliqué que cette initiative vise à relever le niveau des athlètes qui s’entraînent régulièrement. En prélude à cette session, les candidats ont suivi un stage de deux semaines pour mieux se préparer aux différentes épreuves. « Après l’étape de Lomé, ce sera l’étape du nord le 15 novembre prochain, suivie d’une compétition de fin d’année, dont la date sera communiquée ultérieurement. Je voudrais encourager les pratiquants à ne pas lâcher, à continuer les entraînements. Quand on lance des stages, qu’ils viennent pour parfaire leurs mouvements. Sinon, ils risquent de ne pas évoluer », a déclaré le président. Pour l’instructeur et coach international, Dégboé Josélito Léonidase, le niveau des candidats est acceptable, malgré l’interruption des activités depuis plus de deux ans, qui a entraîné un relâchement chez certains athlètes. Il a invité les bonnes volontés à soutenir les clubs en organisant des compétitions interclubs ou des tournois à quatre ou huit participants. Selon lui, ces rencontres offrent aux jeunes pratiquants des occasions de se mesurer et de maintenir leur condition physique. Il a toutefois souligné la nécessité d’informer la fédération du bien-fondé de toute compétition avant son organisation. ATOP/AR/AO

items.title: Mahama congratulates Rev. Stephen Wengam on second term as Assemblies of God, Ghana leader
items.description: President John Mahama has congratulated Reverend Dr Stephen Yenusom Wengam on his inauguration for a second four-year term as General Superintendent of the Assemblies of God, Ghana. He commended Rev. Dr Wengam for his transformational leadership during his first term, particularly the implementation of the Church’s Transformation Agenda, which has resulted in the planting of more than 2,000 churches and the training of over 440 pastors. President Mahama, who is a member of the Assemblies of God, Ghana, together with First Lady Lordina Mahama, gave the commendation at the inauguration of Rev. Dr Wengam and members of the Church’s Executive Presbytery in Accra. He said Rev. Dr Wengam’s re-election reflected the confidence the Church had in his leadership and the work he had undertaken over the past four years. “You have earned that confidence through years of ministry, relationships that have been built across congregations, and work undertaken with your colleagues. Over the past four years, we have planted over 2,000 churches, and trained more than 440 pastors,” he said. The President noted that the achievements were the result of the collective commitment of ministers, congregations and communities that had embraced new missions and ministry opportunities. He said the second term offered the General Superintendent an opportunity to consolidate the gains made during his first tenure while ensuring that the benefits of the Church’s reforms reached congregations across the country. “A second term is a time to deepen worthwhile reforms and ensure that progress reaches the local congregations, including the small assemblies far from the national headquarters. “The confidence shown in your re-election also entails a renewed obligation to listen. May those who work closely with you feel free to offer honest advice and counsel.” President Mahama said the inauguration theme, “The Transformation Agenda Continues “ , anchored on the Six Rs: Reach, Rebuild, Restore, Reform, Reposition and Rebrand, challenged the Church to sustain its progress with patience and purpose. He observed that while the work of the Church was often celebrated from the pulpit, much of its ministry took place away from public attention through missionary journeys, counselling, visits to the sick and service to communities with limited resources. He therefore stressed the importance of prioritising the welfare of pastors and their families, including retired ministers who had devoted their lives to the Church. The President commended the First Lady and her Lordina Foundation for their support towards the healthcare needs of retired pastors through regular health screening exercises. “I salute my wife, First Lady Lordina Mahama, and her Lordina Foundation for the health screening ministry that they undertake every three months with retired pastors,” he said. “Their health screening, counselling, and medication have been a critical lifeline for many of our aged pastors.” President Mahama also underscored the need for strong administrative structures, transparent procedures, responsible financial management and effective leadership succession to ensure the Church’s long-term sustainability. He said the true measure of leadership was not only in the achievements recorded during one’s tenure but also in the people equipped to sustain the work after that leader had left office. The President further commended Rev. Dr Wengam for improving the public image and standing of the Assemblies of God, Ghana. “And I can speak confidently, Assemblies of God Ghana has become one of the most popular and most favoured Pentecostal denominations in Ghana,” the President said. He urged the Church to ensure that its efforts to reposition and rebrand the denomination were reflected in the experiences of members and visitors. “And so, as you continue your work of repositioning and rebranding the church, may the experience of those who enter its doors give meaning to its public image.” He expressed the hope that everyone who entered an Assemblies of God congregation would encounter a welcoming community, sound biblical teaching and support during difficult times. President Mahama also described the history of the Assemblies of God, Ghana, as a remarkable story of faith, perseverance and growth. Tracing its origins to Yendi in 1931, he said the Church had expanded across the country through the dedication of missionaries, Ghanaian ministers and committed congregations. With the denomination expected to celebrate its centenary in 2031, the President expressed confidence that the proposed Centenary Village project would be completed ahead of the milestone. “We shall build it to the glory of God. We honour all former generals, lieutenants, and all those whose service laid the foundation upon which today’s leadership is building,” he said. He stressed that institutions could only endure when successive generations received their inheritance with gratitude and built on it responsibly. Chairman of the World Assemblies of God Fellowship and General Superintendent of the Assemblies of God of Singapore, Reverend Dominic Yeo delivered the homily and conducted the inauguration ceremony. He charged Rev. Dr Wengam and the newly inaugurated Executive Presbytery to remain committed to advancing the Kingdom of God through the ministry of the Assemblies of God, Ghana. In his inaugural address, Rev. Dr Wengam pledged to accelerate the implementation of the Church’s Transformation Agenda, which is built around the Six Rs: Reach, Rebuild, Restore, Reform, Reposition and Rebrand. Other members of the Executive Presbytery inaugurated alongside him were Rev. Kwadwo Boateng Bempeh, Assistant General Superintendent; Rev. Albert Anane, General Secretary; and Rev. Dr Simon Abu Baba, General Treasurer.

items.title: Moyen-Mono : Kativou doté d’un forage et d’un réseau électrique
items.description: Tohoun, 8 nov. (ATOP) – Un forage et un réseau électrique ont été réceptionnés le samedi 7 novembre à Kativou, à 5 km au nord-est de Kpékplémé, dans la commune Moyen-Mono 2. Ces deux infrastructures, réalisées pour un coût total de 32 310 000 F CFA, viennent améliorer les conditions de vie des populations en facilitant l’accès à l’eau potable et à l’électricité. Les ouvrages ont été offerts par Miss Togo 2026, Eyou Prudence Angèle, avec l’appui financier de son partenaire Moov Africa. Le forage, d’une profondeur de 90 mètres, est équipé d’un château d’eau de 7 mètres de hauteur, d’un polytank d’une capacité de 2 m³, avec une possibilité d’extension de 2 m³ supplémentaires, et de trois robinets. Le réseau électrique, d’une puissance de 50 KVA, couvre une distance de 355 mètres. Ces réalisations visent à faciliter l’accès à l’eau potable et à améliorer l’éclairage du village. Elles offriront également aux élèves de meilleures conditions pour réviser leurs cours, notamment en soirée. La représentante de Moov Africa, Léaticia Sanvée, a expliqué que le choix de Kativou répond aux difficultés rencontrées par les ménages pour accéder à l’eau potable. Cette initiative vise à améliorer leurs conditions de vie, à réduire les infections liées à la consommation d’eau insalubre et à soutenir le développement local. Au nom des bénéficiaires, le préfet du Moyen-Mono, Colonel Gnakaoufré Yao Eindrè, et le maire de Moyen-Mono 2, Edou Zomblèwouh, ont salué le geste des donateurs. Ils se sont engagés à veiller au bon entretien des infrastructures et à leur utilisation judicieuse. ATOP/TM/YM/AO

items.title: Military neutralises 60 terrorists, rescues 42 kidnap victims
items.description: … Arrests 56 suspected collaborators, logistics suppliers in nationwide operations By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Armed Forces have neutralised 60 terrorists, rescued 42 kidnapped victims and arrested 56 suspected terrorist collaborators, arms dealers and logistics suppliers in a series of joint military operations across the country in one week. The operations also led to the surrender of more than 15 terrorists and their family members, as well as the recovery of several weapons, ammunition and other items from criminal hideouts. The Director of Defence Media Operations, Major General Michael Onoja, disclosed this in an operational update, saying troops recorded significant successes across the North-East, North-West, North-Central and South-East geopolitical zones. He said troops successfully repelled terrorist attacks at Buni Yadi in Yobe State and Bitta in Borno State, neutralising more than 50 terrorists in the engagements. Onoja also disclosed that troops overran kidnappers’ hideouts in Edimogbo and Obele forests in Kogi State, recovering weapons and other items, while operations in Kwara, Kebbi, Niger, Abia and Anambra states resulted in the rescue of several kidnapped victims, including a baby. Giving details of the operations, he said troops of Operation Hadin Kai, on October 29, 2026, repelled terrorists who approached Buni Yadi in Gujba Local Government Area of Yobe State from the Timbuktu Triangle axis. A follow-up operation on October 30 led to the recovery of 48 terrorist bodies, 42 AK-47 rifles, five PKT machine guns, four general-purpose machine guns, one 60mm mortar, 105 magazines and two video cameras. On October 31, troops operating around Apama and Jauro Bashir, along the terrorists’ withdrawal route, recovered three more bodies, an AK-47 rifle and 188 rounds of ammunition. The same day, terrorists attempted to infiltrate a military position at Bitta in Gwoza Local Government Area of Borno State but were forced to retreat. According to Onoja, subsequent exploitation of the area resulted in the recovery of seven terrorist bodies, four AK-47 rifles, an RPG tube, four RPG bombs, three RPG chargers, a PKM machine gun and a radio. He said 12 terrorist fighters and their family members surrendered between November 2 and 4 at New Abaram Resettlement Village, Banki Junction in Bama LGA and near Ngurusoye in Gwoza LGA of Borno State. The surrendering terrorists reportedly cited sustained military pressure and disagreements between rival JAS and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) factions. On November 2, troops also rescued a female abductee who escaped from the Mandara Mountains at Hudugum, Hambagda, along the Gwoza-Limankara Road. Onoja said troops arrested 50 suspected terrorists, collaborators and logistics suppliers in the North-East, including suppliers and informants at Benisheikh in Kaga LGA on October 31 and November 2. He added that three suppliers at Damboa and two suspected fighters from the Diffa region of Niger Republic were intercepted at Garin Gada in Yunusari LGA of Yobe State on November 3 while allegedly attempting to procure logistics for terrorists operating along the Nigeria-Niger border. On November 5, troops and operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency conducted search operations at several motor parks in Maiduguri to disrupt terrorist supply networks, leading to the arrest of 36 suspects. North-West In the North-West, troops of Operation Fansan Yamma, acting on a distress call from Ribah in Danko/Wasagu LGA of Kebbi State on October 30, cleared the Ribah-Dirindaji Road. A subsequent search-and-rescue operation and night pursuit towards Rambo Village forced terrorists to abandon seven kidnapped victims. On October 31, troops patrolling the Wasagu-Falfala Road in the same local government area responded to an ambush, forcing the attackers to flee and abandon four victims abducted from their farms in Wasagu Village. Onoja said troops also rescued seven kidnapped victims from Sabon Tunga and Binoni villages in Danko-Wasagu LGA on November 3, following search-and-rescue operations around Geso and Ayan Geso in Maru LGA of Zamfara State. On November 2, two suspects allegedly involved in kidnapping and cattle rustling were arrested at Sabon Gida Village in Chikun LGA of Kaduna State. Similarly, troops and operatives of the Department of State Services on November 5 apprehended a suspected terrorist who reportedly sneaked into a clinic in Kagarko LGA of Kaduna State to receive treatment for gunshot wounds sustained during a clash with a rival faction. North-Central In the North-Central, troops of Operation Enduring Peace, during stop-and-search operations at Kukawa Village in Kanam LGA on November 4, intercepted a suspected terrorist with an AK-47 magazine and a round of 7.62mm special ammunition. Preliminary interrogation reportedly revealed that the suspect belonged to a terrorist syndicate allegedly led by one Kaura. Onoja said troops of Operation Whirl Stroke, on November 2, conducted a fighting patrol to a criminal hideout in Edimogbo Forest, where they engaged suspected kidnappers who subsequently fled into the forest. A search of the hideout led to the recovery of 1,000 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, seven bandoliers, six motorcycles and a mobile phone, while the hideout was subsequently destroyed. During further patrols on November 3, troops engaged two suspected kidnappers and neutralised them, recovering two AK-47 rifles, seven magazines and more than 5,000 rounds of ammunition. On November 4, troops conducting operations in Obele Forest neutralised three suspected kidnappers and recovered four AK-47 rifles, 12 magazines, 336 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition and three bandoliers. In another operation on the same day, troops at Jeb Jeb Village in Karim Lamido LGA of Taraba State responded to a distress call over a kidnapping, engaged the attackers and rescued six civilians, including a baby. The Defence spokesman further disclosed that troops on November 1 arrested a wanted member of the Konyo Boys bandit group at Ahmadu Village in Takum LGA of Taraba State. The suspect reportedly led troops to a hut where an AK-47 rifle and a mobile phone were recovered. On November 4, a terrorist, his wife and two children surrendered to troops at Atsawa in Lokoja LGA of Kogi State with an AK-47 rifle, four rounds of ammunition and a radio. They reportedly attributed their decision to surrender to sustained military offensives against terrorist camps in Agbaja and Kakanda forests. The same day, troops at Jamata in Lokoja LGA arrested a suspected logistics supplier who allegedly confessed to conveying supplies to terrorists loyal to the late Kachallah Baccujo in Agbaja Forest. On November 5, troops also arrested a suspected gunrunner in Gboko LGA of Benue State. In Niger State, troops of Operation Savannah Shield, following sustained patrols around Rijiyan Nagwamatse in Kontagora LGA on November 5, engaged suspected bandits and rescued 15 kidnapped victims. The troops also recovered two AK-47 rifles, seven rifle magazines, three RPG bombs, 33 motorcycles, N4.105 million and ammunition. Onoja said troops and members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, on November 4, ambushed Ansaru terrorists who invaded Nanu Village in Kaiama LGA of Kwara State, neutralising two of them. In another operation on the same day, troops at Gulbin Boka, Barbada, in Dusai Ward of Mariga LGA, Niger State, pursued fleeing kidnappers and arrested an injured suspect at Dusai Village. The suspect reportedly disclosed that three persons were involved in the attempted kidnapping. Also on November 4, troops on a fighting patrol in Lema-Ndeji Forest in Edu LGA of Kwara State rescued three kidnapped victims who had escaped from their captors. South-East In the South-East, troops of Operation Udoka on November 4 rescued a kidnapped victim at Isuochi following an attack by gunmen on a compound at Okwe Ubahu Nneato in Umunneochi LGA of Abia State. In Anambra State, troops on November 2 searched a shop near the Marine Outpost at Otuocha in Anambra East LGA, following intelligence that a suspect was allegedly concealing weapons used to intimidate members of the community. The operation led to the recovery of a pump-action rifle, a damaged hunting rifle and 13 cartridges. CDS commends troops Reacting to the operational successes, the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, commended troops for their courage, resilience and sacrifices in the various theatres of operation. Onoja, who conveyed the CDS’s message on behalf of the Armed Forces of Nigeria, said Oluyede honoured the memory of an officer, a soldier and a civilian hunter who lost their lives in the line of duty while supporting military operations. The CDS assured their families that their sacrifices would remain indelible in the nation’s memory and wished wounded personnel speedy and full recovery. He also appreciated the contributions of other security agencies, emphasising the need for sustained collaboration, effective intelligence sharing and coordinated operational planning to consolidate the gains recorded. Oluyede called on traditional rulers, community leaders and other stakeholders to strengthen their partnership with security agencies by providing timely and credible information on suspicious movements and activities through the nearest military formation or the toll-free emergency line 193. He urged citizens to deny criminals access to logistics and other forms of support, while warning against mob action, misinformation and the spread of disinformation. The CDS further charged troops to remain vigilant, disciplined and combat-ready, stressing that terrorists and other criminal elements remained dangerous even when wounded or under pressure. He reaffirmed the Armed Forces’ commitment to sustaining ongoing operations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders until lasting peace, security and stability are restored across the country. The post Military neutralises 60 terrorists, rescues 42 kidnap victims appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Ndèye Khady Anna Diatta offre au Sénégal sa troisième médaille d’or
items.description: Le Sénégal poursuit sa moisson de médailles d’or aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. Ndèye Khady Anna Diatta vient de décrocher le troisième titre olympique du pays hôte, à l’issue de son parcours victorieux en lutte de plage, dans la catégorie des moins de 45 kg. La jeune Sénégalaise confirme ainsi les espoirs placés en elle. Âgée de 17 ans, elle réalise un parcours remarquable avec un carton plein dans sa compétition, enchaînant les victoires face à ses adversaires. Porte-drapeau de la délégation sénégalaise lors de ces Jeux, Ndèye Khady Anna Diatta apporte une nouvelle consécration au Sénégal, après les titres remportés par Élisabeth Diatta chez les moins de 55 kg et Maguette Diop dans la catégorie des moins de 80 kg. items.title: Train collision in Egypt's Giza kills 4, injures 88: health ministry
items.description: Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday, derailing several carriages, killing four and injuring dozens, according to the authorities. Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan. The health ministry said an initial count put the toll from the crash at four passengers killed, with 88 others currently being treated for injuries in hospitals around the Giza area. State-owned media had earlier reported 120 people were wounded, without clarifying the degree of injury. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident “with great concern”, and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”. Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said. Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza’s Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar extended condolences to Egypt in the wake of the “tragic” accident, particularly the bereaved families. “Our thoughts and prayers are with those injured, and we wish them a swift and full recovery,” he said. “Pakistan stands in solidarity with Egypt and its people during this difficult time.” In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo. In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens . Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents . Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

items.title: Two trains collide in Egypt, killing four people and injuring dozens more, authorities say
items.description: At least four people have been killed and nearly 90 injured after two trains collided in Egypt, the health ministry says. Several carriages were derailed after one train collided with the rear of another between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Giza, near the capital Cairo, the Egyptian National Railways Authority said in a statement. Dozens of ambulances were dispatched to transport the injured to nearby hospitals, while cranes were deployed to remove the wreckage after traffic on the railroad was disrupted, Egyptian authorities said. The Egyptian railway system, the oldest in Africa and the Middle East, has a long history of deadly accidents, including when a train lost control while approaching the main station in Ramses, igniting a fire that killed 25 people. Another occurred in 2017 on the way to Alexandria, when a train derailed and collided head-on with another train, killing more than 40 people.

items.title: Chavirement d’une pirogue à Lompoul : le président Diomaye Faye présente ses condoléances aux familles des victimes
items.description: Le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, a exprimé sa compassion à la suite du chavirement d’une pirogue au large de Lompoul, dans la commune de Léona, département de Kébémer. Dans un message publié sur sa page Facebook, il a présenté ses condoléances aux familles des victimes et assuré que les moyens de l’État sont mobilisés pour retrouver les personnes portées disparues. « Je m'incline devant la mémoire des victimes et présente mes condoléances attristées à leurs familles et aux populations de Kébémer », a écrit le chef de l’État. Il a également adressé une pensée aux rescapés ainsi qu’aux personnes dans l’attente de nouvelles de leurs proches. Le président de la République a, par ailleurs, assuré que toutes les autorités et les ressources nécessaires sont mobilisées pour mener les opérations de recherche, porter assistance aux survivants et accompagner les familles éprouvées par ce drame. Revenant sur la question des départs par voie maritime, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye a réaffirmé la détermination de l’État à lutter contre les réseaux qui organisent ces traversées irrégulières. Il a également insisté sur la nécessité de créer des perspectives pour la jeunesse afin de réduire les départs à la recherche de meilleures conditions de vie à l’étranger. « Aucun départ ne devrait avoir la mer pour seul horizon », a-t-il notamment déclaré, réaffirmant la volonté des autorités de poursuivre les efforts dans la lutte contre l’émigration irrégulière.

Beyond alcohol sponsorship: Governance, accountability and the language of leadership in Ghana football
items.description: Recent comments by the President of the Ghana Football Association (GFA) before Parliament’s Select Committee on Sports have rekindled an important conversation about the future of football governance in Ghana. Central to the discussion was the appeal for a review of restrictions on alcohol sponsorship in sport, accompanied by the assertion that Ghana football lost a potential US$5 million sponsorship opportunity from Guinness Ghana. While the financial implications of such restrictions deserve serious consideration, the broader issues raised by the testimony extend beyond sponsorship revenue. They speak to leadership, institutional responsibility, and the language through which sports administrator’s position themselves in relation to the national game. The Sponsorship Argument: A Question of Diversification No serious observer would deny that sponsorship remains a critical pillar of modern sport financing. Across Africa and the world, sponsorship agreements support player development, competition organization, infrastructure investment, and grassroots participation. In a football economy often characterized by resource constraints, every funding opportunity matters. However, framing alcohol sponsorship as a necessary solution risks oversimplifying the economic realities of contemporary football administration. Globally, football organizations increasingly rely on diversified revenue streams, including media rights, digital content partnerships, telecommunications sponsorships, financial services partnerships, merchandising, licensing, government support, international grants, and fan engagement initiatives. The sustainability of a football association should not be dependent upon the availability or absence of one category of corporate sponsor. The key policy question therefore is not whether football should generate revenue. Rather, it is whether football governance structures have sufficiently explored innovative and socially responsible financing alternatives before advocating the relaxation of public health restrictions. This is particularly important in Ghana, where concerns about alcohol consumption among young people continue to attract public health attention. Sporting institutions occupy a unique social position. They are not merely commercial entities but cultural institutions that influence values, behaviors, and aspirations. Decisions regarding sponsorship should therefore balance economic benefits against wider social responsibilities. Football’s Social Contract Sport enjoys legitimacy because society grants it special status. The public invests emotionally, financially, and politically in national teams and sporting competitions. In return, sports organizations are expected to act as responsible custodians of public trust. This social contract becomes especially significant when discussing partnerships involving products that may have public health implications. While alcohol companies have historically invested significantly in sports sponsorship worldwide, legitimate questions remain regarding the long-term alignment between public health objectives and marketing through sport. The issue is therefore not simply one of lost revenue. It is about determining what kind of commercial relationships best serve football’s developmental mission, while protecting the welfare of the communities it seeks to inspire. The Language of Leadership Matters Perhaps equally revealing was the reported reference to the Black Stars as “your Black Stars” during the parliamentary engagement. At first glance, some may dismiss this as an insignificant choice of words. Yet within governance studies, leadership communication is rarely viewed as trivial. Language shapes perceptions of ownership, responsibility, and accountability. The Black Stars are Ghana’s most visible sporting institution. While the team belongs symbolically to all Ghanaians, the GFA has been entrusted with its administration and strategic development. Consequently, stakeholders naturally expect football leaders to identify closely with both the successes and challenges of the national team. The phrase “your Black Stars” introduces an interesting dynamic. Whether intentional or not, it may be interpreted as creating distance between football administrators and the team they govern. It potentially shifts ownership towards Parliament, government, or the public while reducing the perceived accountability of football leadership. By contrast, language such as “our Black Stars” conveys collective stewardship. It signals a shared commitment among administrators, government, players, and supporters toward national football development. Leadership communication is particularly important in contexts where public confidence in football governance has fluctuated. During periods of scrutiny, stakeholders often evaluate not only policy decisions but also the symbolism contained in leaders’ words. Stewardship versus Administration At the heart of these debates lies a more fundamental question: What does football leadership mean? If leadership is understood merely as administration, then success may be measured through budgets, sponsorship contracts, and operational efficiency. However, if leadership is understood as stewardship, then it requires something more. Stewardship demands accountability, collective ownership, and a willingness to project unity around the institutions being managed. It recognizes that football administrators are temporary custodians of assets that ultimately belong to the wider public. In this regard, both the sponsorship argument and the “your Black Stars” statement reveal a common tension. They raise questions about how football leadership perceives its relationship with the game. Is football governance primarily focused on securing resources from external actors? Or is it equally committed to strengthening public trust, institutional legitimacy, and collective responsibility? A Way Forward Rather than polarizing the debate into supporters and opponents of alcohol sponsorship, Ghanaian football would benefit from a broader conversation about sustainable sport financing. Such a conversation should include: Diversification of sponsorship portfolios beyond alcohol-related industries. Greater investment in digital commercialization and fan engagement. Stronger collaboration between football authorities, public health experts, and policymakers. Enhanced transparency regarding sponsorship negotiations and funding strategies. Leadership communication that reinforces collective ownership and accountability. Football’s future cannot be built solely on the size of sponsorship deals. It must also be built on public confidence in the institutions that govern the game. Conclusion The recent parliamentary engagement should be viewed as more than a discussion about a lost sponsorship opportunity. It offers an opportunity to reflect on the broader governance philosophies shaping Ghanaian football. The challenge facing football leadership is not simply to maximize revenue. It is to demonstrate that commercial ambitions can coexist with social responsibility, public accountability, and inclusive stewardship. Similarly, leadership language should reinforce shared ownership of the national game rather than unintentionally creating distance from it. Ultimately, the debate is not about alcohol sponsorship alone. It is about how football leaders define their responsibilities to the sport, the state, and the millions of Ghanaians who regard the Black Stars as a national symbol that belongs to all of us.

items.title: PML-N retains Sahiwal's PP-203 as per unofficial result; counting underway in Gujranwala's NA-77
items.description: LAHORE: The ruling PML-N retained Sahiwal’s Punjab Assembly constituency PP-203 in Sunday’s by-election, while counting was underway in Gujranwala’s National Assembly constituency NA-77. Both seats had fallen vacant after the deaths of their respective lawmakers in September. Polling in the constituencies began at 8am and concluded at 5pm, with the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) reporting an uninterrupted and largely peaceful process. In PP-203 of Chichawatni, PML-N’s Muhammad Asad Hanif Jutt won with 42,114 votes, defeating his closest rival, Muhammad Awais Mahmood of Tehreek-i-Ehsas Pakistan (TEP), who secured 24,512 votes, according to the Form-47 seen by Dawn . The margin of victory was 17,602 votes, while voter turnout stood at 27.6 per cent. Form-47 is the provisional consolidated statement of results of the vote count of all polling stations in a constituency, prepared by the returning officer (RO) concerned. The by-poll was held following the death of PML-N MPA Chaudhry Muhammad Hanif Jutt. This was the second time that a by-election was held in the constituency after the 2024 general elections. In NA-77, PML-N candidate Rashid Basheer Virk was among 11 candidates contesting for the seat left vacant after the Sept 11 demise of his father, Chaudhry Mehmood Bashir Virk, a five-time MNA. The available results had yet to establish the final outcome in the constituency. Both by-elections were marked by a low voter turnout, while notices were also issued to several PML-N lawmakers for alleged violations of the election code, mostly over visiting polling stations in the two constituencies. Chief Election Commissioner Sikander Sultan Raja also visited the provincial election chief’s office, where he was briefed on the polling process in both constituencies, ECP said . After the balloting process concluded, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, whose PML-N is in power in the province, made multiple posts on X, claiming her party was in the lead in both NA-77 and PP-203 . In one post, CM Maryam wrote, “This electoral victory is no ordinary victory. It is a resounding public rebuke to conspiracy peddlers, hate mongers and those who refuse to read the writing on the wall.” She contended that the results portrayed that the “politics of delivery is far more enduring than the politics of hate and revenge”. “I am glad politics has returned to delivery and performance. Wake up and smell the coffee… or keep sleeping in denial!” the PML-N leader added. Notices over alleged electoral conduct violations While the polling was under way, notices, copies of which are available with Dawn , were issued to Punjab MPA Qudsia Batool, MNA Saira Afzal Tarar and Parliamentary Secretary for Information and Culture Shazia Rizwan for alleged violation of the Code of Conduct after reports emerged on social media that the three had visited various polling stations within NA-77, a statement issued by the office of the provincial election commissioner said. Notices were also issued over alleged violations of the Code of Conduct to PML-N’s MNA Syeda Nosheen Iftikhar and MPA Hina Arshad Warraich for allegedly visiting polling stations. The officials were directed to appear at the Election Complex in Gujranwala for an explanation at 3pm. Separately, PML-N leader and Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari claimed in a post on X that supporters of Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) candidate Qazi Ibrahim Gujjar were caught “openly stamping ballots” with the election commission staff present. Acting on the complaint, the provincial election commissioner said the returning officer concerned has been directed to probe the matter and submit a report. On Saturday, the ECP took notice of an alleged violation of the Code of Conduct by Information Minister Attaullah Tarar during by-election campaigning in NA-77 . According to a cause list issued on Sunday, Tarar, along with Virk, Batool and others, has been summoned to appear at the next hearing on Nov 12. According to the ECP, the minister visited the constituency by helicopter and addressed a campaign event for Rashid, violating a provision in the Code of Conduct , which bars public office holders from participating in campaign activities. ECP has sought a report from the district monitoring officer and the district returning officer to inquire into the matter. The watchdog also said that the result of the constituency could be withheld until a final decision is made on the matter. Meanwhile, notices were also issued to PML-N MPAs Malik Qasim Nadeem and Motiya Begum for allegedly visiting several polling stations in Chichawatni’s PP-203 on the polling day. The notices issued by the district monitoring officer, seen by Dawn , accused both of violating Para 48 of the Code of Conduct, which bars “all kinds of campaigns” and canvassing within a 400-metre radius of a polling station. The MPAs were asked to appear either in person or through counsel at the Municipal Committee Office at 5pm on Nov 9 (Monday) to clarify their position. Polling in PP-203 The seat was initially won in 2024 by independent candidate Rai Murtaza Iqbal, backed by the PTI, with 55,874 votes against Jutt, who polled 35,163 votes. However, Iqbal, along with four other PTI-backed parliamentarians, was disqualified and denotified by the ECP following their conviction by an anti-terrorism court in Faisalabad on July 31. Subsequently, the ECP scheduled a by-election for Nov 23, 2025, which was won by Jutt with 46,820 votes. His closest rival, independent candidate Falik Sher, secured 10,975 votes. Jutt died of cardiac arrest on Sept 17 this year, necessitating Sunday’s by-election in the constituency. Around 1,370 polling personnel, including 574 women and 796 men, were deputed at 185 polling stations across the constituency. District Police Officer Usman Tipu said 1,100 personnel had been deployed to ensure security during the by-election. A total of 185 polling stations had been established in the constituency, including 11 in Category A, 37 in Category B and 137 in Category C. A comprehensive traffic management plan had also been devised, with more than 65 personnel assigned duties.

items.title: Keyamo launches aviation campaign series ahead of 2027 elections
items.description: By Okeremu Samuel The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, has launched a television campaign series highlighting the aviation sector’s achievements under President Bola Tinubu’s administration ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Tagged Tinubu Aviation Revolution Series, the initiative features short television presentations showcasing the administration’s aviation policies, infrastructure development and efforts to reposition the sector as a driver of economic growth. Keyamo announced the initiative on his social media platforms following his appointment as Director of Air Transport Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council. The series commenced broadcasting on major television stations on November 1 and is expected to run until shortly before the presidential election. The initiative places aviation among the sectors being highlighted in the administration’s performance campaign, given its strategic role in facilitating international trade, tourism, investment, employment and economic connectivity. Under the Tinubu administration, the aviation sector has pursued reforms and infrastructure upgrades covering airport facilities, safety oversight, aircraft financing and international connectivity. The ongoing rehabilitation and modernisation of airport infrastructure, alongside efforts to improve operational efficiency, are among the developments being showcased in the television presentations. The campaign also adopts a sector-specific approach to communicating the administration’s record, using developments in aviation to highlight policies and projects with implications for business, air travel and national economic activities. As political activities ahead of the 2027 elections gather momentum, the series is expected to form part of the APC’s efforts to communicate the administration’s achievements and policies to Nigerians. The initiative comes as political parties and their campaign organisations intensify efforts to present their records, programmes and policy priorities to the electorate ahead of the next general election. items.title: Anié/Chefferie traditionnelle : M. Otoundé Tchédji reçoit son décret de reconnaissance
items.description: Anié, 8 nov. (ATOP) – M. Otoundé Tchédji, désigné chef du canton d’Atchinédji, dans la commune d’Anié 2, a reçu, le vendredi 6 novembre, son décret de reconnaissance. Il porte désormais le nom de Dada Fesso Tchédji V. La cérémonie a été présidée par le gouverneur de la région des Plateaux, Gal. Dadja Manganawé. En remettant le décret au nouveau chef, le gouverneur a indiqué que la reconnaissance officielle d’un chef traditionnel consacre son rôle dans la préservation des valeurs culturelles et du patrimoine traditionnel. Il a précisé que cet acte, signé par le Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé, autorise Otoundé Tchédji à exercer ses fonctions de chef du canton d’Atchinédji. Le Gal. Manganawé a rappelé que le chef traditionnel contribue à la cohésion sociale, à la préservation des us et coutumes ainsi qu’à la promotion de la paix et de la stabilité au sein des communautés. Il joue également un rôle d’arbitrage et de conciliation dans les conflits relevant des traditions. Le chef est aussi consulté sur les questions de développement local, notamment en matière d’environnement, de santé, de foncier, de sécurité et d’éducation. Il doit, à cet effet, faire preuve de loyauté envers l’État, de neutralité et d’impartialité, tout en restant apolitique. Le maire de la commune Anié 2, Gossou Kokou, a souligné l’importance stratégique et institutionnelle de la chefferie traditionnelle dans la mise en œuvre des actions publiques auprès des populations. Il a présenté cette institution comme un trait d’union entre le gouvernement central et les communautés rurales, avant d’inviter le nouveau chef à faire preuve d’intégrité et d’impartialité dans l’exercice de ses fonctions. Dada Fesso Tchédji V a déclaré compter sur la contribution de tous pour bien accomplir sa mission. Il a salué la volonté du président du Conseil de rapprocher le pouvoir des administrés et de promouvoir le travail dans un esprit d’unité. Le nouveau chef a également souhaité l’accompagnement des autorités communales et régionales. La cérémonie a été marquée par des prestations folkloriques des groupes « Adjigo », « Kabyè-Losso » et « Peulh » du canton d’Atchinédji, puis une animation musicale assurée par l’artiste Gbèdo. ATOP/KV/AO

items.title: Privée de patrie, de soins et de comptes bancaires : Nathalie Yamb explique son calvaire au quotidien et fustige le renouvellement des sanctions de l’UE contre sa personne
items.description: Visée depuis le 26 juin 2025 par des sanctions de l'Union européenne, la militante et analyste politique helvético-camerounaise Nathalie Yamb a vu ces mesures restrictives reconduites le 9 octobre 2026 au titre des « activités déstabilisatrices de la Russie ». Dans une longue tribune au vitriol, l'activiste panafricaniste dénonce un acharnement administratif extrajudiciaire qui bouleverse son existence : comptes bancaires clôturés, interdiction d’accès au système de paiement international, impossibilité de regagner son domicile en Suisse ou d'assister sa famille, et suspension de ses soins médicaux. Entre griefs diplomatiques liés à sa proximité avec le Niger ou ses prises de position sur l'Ukraine, elle dépeint les rouages d'une mort sociale et financière qu'elle qualifie de véritable « châtiment à la Sisyphe ». Le bras de fer diplomatique entre Bruxelles et les figures du panafricanisme contemporain vient de franchir un nouveau cap. Le 9 octobre 2026, l’Union européenne a formellement renouvelé l'arsenal de sanctions adopté à l'encontre de Nathalie Yamb, initialement décrété le 26 juin 2025. Inscrites sous le régime juridique de la répression des « activités déstabilisatrices de la Russie », ces dispositions ciblent, selon la militante, son influence publique, ses conférences et ses analyses géopolitiques en faveur de la souveraineté africaine. Se déclarant à la fois suissesse et africaine, résidant hors de l'UE et sans avoirs sur son sol, elle pointe l'incohérence d'une mesure européenne qui s'applique à elle alors même que Berne n'a pas repris ces sanctions à son compte. Au quotidien, le couperet des sanctions s'est traduit par une mise au ban intégrale du système économique moderne. Nathalie Yamb détaille un effet domino dévastateur : gel puis fermeture unilatérale de ses comptes en Suisse accusant notamment la Bank Cler d'avoir confisqué ses avoirs, désactivation de toutes ses cartes bancaires et clôture de ses comptes financiers en Afrique. Le blocage s'étend de manière spectaculaire à l'écosystème numérique mondial : plateformes de cryptomonnaies (Binance, Kraken), services de transfert (Paypal, Stripe, Wise), cagnottes participatives (GoFundMe) et géants du commerce électronique ou du divertissement (Amazon, Airbnb, Booking, Ebay, Netflix, Spotify) ont tous fermé ses accès. Privée également des monétisations de ses contenus sur Facebook, YouTube et X, l'analyste affirme ne plus pouvoir régler son loyer, payer ses honoraires d'avocats, honorer son assurance maladie ou poursuivre ses traitements médicaux en raison du refus des établissements bancaires d'exécuter des paiements émis en son nom. Au-delà des entraves matérielles, l'impact humain et familial constitue l'un des volets les plus éprouvants du témoignage. Frappée d'une interdiction de transit et d'entrée sur le territoire de l'UE, mais surtout d'une interdiction de survol de l'espace aérien européen, Nathalie Yamb se trouve dans l'incapacité physique de regagner son domicile en Suisse, pays totalement enclavé au milieu des États membres de l'Union. Ce blocus géographique a entraîné une rupture brutale de ses liens intimes : bloquée hors d'Europe lors de l'instauration des sanctions, elle n'a toujours pas pu rencontrer son premier petit-enfant né cette année, n'a pu assister aux 80 ans de sa mère et se trouve privée de la possibilité de veiller sur elle lors d'une intervention chirurgicale programmée l'an prochain. Sur le fond du dossier, les motifs officiels retenus pour justifier la prolongation des sanctions témoignent de l'imbrication étroite entre parole politique et mesures coercitives. Parmi les éléments invoqués figurent son allocution prononcée au sommet Russie-Afrique de Sotchi en 2019, une vidéo de 2023 critiquant l'opération Wuambushu à Mayotte, sa nomination comme conseillère spéciale du président de la République du Niger assortie d'un passeport diplomatique, ainsi qu'une publication de 2025 fustigeant la politique de l'Ukraine au Sahel. Face à ce qu'elle qualifie de sanctions purement extrajudiciaires, la requérante dénonce l'impasse des voies de recours devant le Tribunal de l'Union européenne : une procédure contentieuse exige plus d'une année pour obtenir une audience, et le délibéré favorable qui pourrait en résulter est immédiatement rendu caduc par l'adoption d'un nouvel acte de renouvellement par l'UE. Dénonçant une mécanique sans fin digne du mythe de Sisyphe, Nathalie Yamb conclut néanmoins avec défi : « Ce que vous avez commencé, on va terminer ». L’article Privée de patrie, de soins et de comptes bancaires : Nathalie Yamb explique son calvaire au quotidien et fustige le renouvellement des sanctions de l'UE contre sa personne est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Journée « Togo propre » : Les populations des Savanes mobilisées pour la salubrité publique
items.description: Dapaong, 8 nov. (ATOP) – Les populations de plusieurs communes de la région des Savanes ont pris part, le samedi 7 novembre, aux travaux communautaires d’assainissement organisés dans le cadre de la journée nationale « Togo propre ». Ces actions visent à renforcer les comportements citoyens en matière d’hygiène et à prévenir les risques sanitaires liés à l’insalubrité. La mobilisation a réuni les jeunes, les femmes, les Volontaires d’engagement citoyen (VEC) et les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS). Dans les communes de Tône 1, Kpendjal 1 et 2, Cinkassé 1, Oti 1 et 2 et Oti Sud 1 et 2, les opérations ont concerné les marchés, les établissements publics, les voies et les abords des infrastructures collectives. Munis de matériels de nettoyage, les habitants, accompagnés des autorités administratives, municipales et traditionnelles, ont procédé au balayage, au ramassage des ordures et au désherbage des espaces publics. Les autorités locales ont invité les populations à poursuivre les travaux d’assainissement au-delà de cette journée mensuelle. Elles les ont exhortées à maintenir la propreté des espaces de vie pour préserver la santé de tous. ATOP/JK/AO

items.title: 37e Tour cycliste international du Faso: Triplé inédit pour Paul Daumont sous le regard du Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré
items.description: ‎‎(Ouagadougou, 8 novembre 2026) Le Président du Faso, Chef de l'État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, a présidé ce dimanche la clôture de la 37ᵉ édition du Tour cycliste international du Faso sur le boulevard Thomas-SANKARA. Au terme d’une ultime étape disputée entre Dapelogo et Ouagadougou, conclue par un circuit urbain palpitant de quatre tours de 12 kilomètres, c’est des mains du Chef de l'État que le grand vainqueur, le burkinabè Paul DAUMONT, a reçu l’emblématique maillot jaune. ‎‎La présence du Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ à la ligne d'arrivée a rehaussé l'éclat d'une compétition symbolisant la ténacité, l'excellence et la résilience sportive de toute une Nation. ‎ Accueilli par une foule en liesse massée le long de l'avenue, l'Étalon cycliste a revêtu la tunique jaune sous les acclamations du public. ‎‎Cette 37ᵉ édition s'achève par la victoire d'étape de l'Algérien Azzedine LAGAB et inscrit en lettres d'or Paul DAUMONT dans les annales du cyclisme : avec le maillot sur les épaules, il réalise un triplé consécutif inédit dans l'histoire du Tour Cycliste International du Faso. ‎‎80 coureurs de 14 pays africains et européens ont participé à ce 37e Tour du Faso qui a traversé 8 régions du pays pour une distance totale de 2 387,97 km, dont 1 399,97 km de course effective répartis sur 10 étapes et 988 km de transbordement. ‎‎La direction d de la communication de la Présidence du Faso L’article 37e Tour cycliste international du Faso: Triplé inédit pour Paul Daumont sous le regard du Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Tône/Religion : Radio Maria ouvre ses portes aux auditeurs
items.description: Dapaong, 8 nov. (ATOP) – Radio Maria Dapaong a organisé, le samedi 7 novembre, une journée portes ouvertes à l’intention de ses auditeurs. Cette initiative leur a permis de découvrir les installations de la station, son fonctionnement et les nouveaux équipements acquis. La journée s’inscrit dans la volonté de la radio de consolider sa mission pastorale et de maintenir une relation de proximité avec son public. Elle vise également à renforcer les liens avec les fidèles qui suivent quotidiennement ses programmes. Les visiteurs ont parcouru les différents locaux et découvert les conditions de préparation et de diffusion des émissions. Chacun a également eu l’occasion de passer en direct à l’antenne pour donner ses impressions et saluer ses proches. L’entrée de la station Le directeur de Radio Maria Dapaong, l’abbé Jean Tarboute, a présenté les nouveaux équipements récemment acquis et installés dans la station. Il a précisé que l’ancien matériel est conservé en réserve pour servir en cas de besoin. Selon lui, cette visite permet aux auditeurs de mieux connaître les moyens techniques et financiers nécessaires au fonctionnement de la radio et de comprendre l’importance de leur soutien pour la poursuite de ses activités. L’abbé Jean Tarboute a rappelé que Radio Maria Dapaong est essentiellement une radio d’évangélisation, dont la mission première est de porter la Bonne Nouvelle et la parole de Dieu au-delà des frontières. « À travers ses programmes, la station entend également contribuer à l’information et à la formation de ses auditeurs, tout en favorisant leur rapprochement spirituel avec Dieu », a-t-il expliqué. Une auditrice de la station, Mlle Richala Aboudou, s’est dite charmée par les installations et le travail réalisé au sein de la radio pour le bonheur de ses auditeurs. Radio Maria Dapaong a été créée dans le cadre de l’extension du réseau Radio Maria au Togo, lancé le 19 mars 1997 à l’initiative de l’ancien archevêque de Lomé, Mgr Philippe Fanoko Kpodzro. Implantée dans le diocèse de Dapaong, elle contribue à l’évangélisation des populations de la région des Savanes. La station émet sur la fréquence 88,5 FM. Ses programmes sont axés notamment sur la prière, la liturgie, la catéchèse, la formation humaine et spirituelle, ainsi que sur des thématiques liées à l’éducation, à la santé et au développement communautaire. Au fil des années, elle a renforcé sa présence dans le paysage médiatique régional et poursuivi la modernisation de ses équipements pour améliorer la qualité de ses émissions. ATOP/JK/AO

items.title: Making better money decisions in 2027 (1)
items.description: By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor This year is almost gone. By the time you read this article, there will be 51 days to the end of 2026 and the beginning of 2027. Among other things, a new year, just like a new day, offers new opportunities to achieve something new and make progress. While the year will offer opportunities to make money and become wealthier, the choices made by individuals, households, businesses and nations will determine the level of financial progress and the amount of wealth achieved by the end of the year. For the next few weeks, we will discuss how to make better money decisions in 2027. The first step is to review the money decisions you made in 2026 and honestly answer this question: “Am I wealthier in 2026 than I was in 2025?” To answer this question objectively, ask yourself: How much did I earn, save and invest in 2026? What was the total return on my savings and investments? How much did I borrow? Did I achieve my financial goals? Did I spend according to a budget or as the spirit led me? Did I even have financial goals? If not, why? Did I keep records of all my income and expenses? Your answers will help you determine whether you are wealthier than you were the previous year. The second thing you need to do to make better decisions in 2027 is to set clear financial goals. Your first financial goal must be: “I will record all my financial activities, income and expenses.” This goal is easy to achieve. First, identify what you spend money on regularly and develop a template for daily records. These items include food, essential commodities (bath soap, detergent, toothpaste and dishwashing soap), transport, utility bills, education, rent, clothes, essential services (repairs, parking fees, dry-cleaning and house cleaning), gifts (including alms and offerings), airtime/data, capital projects (television, furniture, car and washing machine) and assets (land, house and shares). Create a note to record the money you earn and spend daily. You can keep it on your phone or laptop, or on paper. A digital device is preferable because you can save the record in your email account and access it anytime, anywhere. (To be continued) The post Making better money decisions in 2027 (1) appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Basketball : deux jeunes talents guinéens U16 entament un parcours de formation de plusieurs années en Grèce
items.description: Deux jeunes basketteurs guinéens, Djouma Bah et Billy Nankouma Diallo, sont arrivés en Grèce où ils bénéficieront d'un programme de formation associant études scolaires et perfectionnement sportif. Cette opportunité fait suite à leur sélection lors d'une détection organisée en Guinée par l'association Basketball Pour Tous, à laquelle avaient pris part de nombreux jeunes talents. Retenus à l'issue de cette sélection, les deux joueurs de la catégorie U16 ont été choisis pour poursuivre leur parcours scolaire et développer leurs compétences sportives dans un environnement international. Leur arrivée en Grèce marque une nouvelle étape dans leur progression et leur ouvre des perspectives de formation et d'épanouissement. Basketball Pour Tous précise qu'il s'agit d'un véritable parcours de formation, et non d'un simple séjour ponctuel. Djouma Bah et Billy Nankouma Diallo prendront part à l'ensemble des activités et des formations prévues dans le cadre de ce programme, qui s'étendra sur plusieurs années. Cette initiative s'inscrit dans la mission de l'association, qui entend contribuer à l'émergence de jeunes talents guinéens en faisant du basketball un levier d'accès à l'éducation, à la formation et aux opportunités internationales. L'objectif est également d'accompagner les jeunes dans la construction d'un parcours durable, au-delà de la seule pratique sportive. Créée par l'ancien international guinéen Aguibou Diallo, ex-joueur du club grec du Panathinaïkos, Basketball Pour Tous œuvre depuis plus de dix ans à l'identification, à l'encadrement et à la promotion des jeunes talents guinéens. À travers ses initiatives, l'association cherche à leur offrir de nouvelles perspectives de développement grâce au sport et à l'éducation. L'organisation a enfin exprimé sa reconnaissance à ses partenaires et à toutes les personnes qui contribuent à la réalisation de cette initiative. Le parcours de Djouma Bah et de Billy Nankouma Diallo illustre ainsi les possibilités qu'un accompagnement structuré peut offrir aux jeunes sportifs guinéens. items.title: Haho : Le chef canton de Kpédomé reçoit son décret de reconnaissance
items.description: Notsè, 8 nov. (ATOP) – Le chef de canton de Kpédomé, dans la commune Haho 3, Ajavon Aboua, a reçu son décret de reconnaissance, le samedi 7 novembre. La cérémonie a été marquée par la procession d’entrée du chef, l’exécution de l’hymne national et des prestations de groupes folkloriques de Kpédomé, d’Agbaladomé et d’Alinou. Elle s’est déroulée en présence du Prof Komi Selom Klassou, président de l’Assemblée nationale. Désormais appelé Togbuigan Adovi Aboua II, il a pour mission de veiller à l’harmonie et à la cohésion sociale. Il dispose d’un pouvoir d’arbitrage et de conciliation des parties en matière d’us et coutumes. Le nouveau chef est également appelé à recevoir l’administration locale et les collectivités décentralisées sur les questions relatives au développement local, notamment l’environnement, la santé, les questions foncières, la sécurité et l’éducation. Il représente sa population dans ses rapports avec l’Etat, les collectivités territoriales et les autres acteurs institutionnels ou sociaux en matière des us et coutumes. En lui remettant le décret, le gouverneur de la région des Plateaux, Général de brigade Dadja Maganawé, l’a exhorté au respect et à la protection des populations dont il est désormais le gardien. Il l’a invité à bannir de son quotidien tout comportement susceptible de compromettre son statut de chef, afin d’accomplir dignement ses fonctions. Le gouverneur a également demandé à la population de respecter l’autorité qu’elle s’est librement donnée, en lui apportant soutien et encouragement dans l’exercice de ses fonctions et dans le développement du canton de Kpédomé. Le maire de Haho 3, Amoudji Komlan, a demandé à Togbuigan Adovi Aboua II d’œuvrer pour assurer une gestion participative de la commune. Les autorités traditionnelles présentes, dont Togbui Kossi Amégnona Adako II, chef de canton de Dalia, ont conseillé au récipiendaire de bien représenter sa population et de rester loyal envers l’État. Elles l’ont également invité à entreprendre des démarches pour obtenir des projets qui contribueront au développement de son canton. Le nouveau chef a exprimé sa volonté de servir la population de Kpédomé dans la paix, de rester fidèle dans la gestion des affaires du canton et d’exécuter dignement ses tâches de chef de canton, en toute responsabilité. Il a salué le soutien des autorités locales, traditionnelles et politiques, notamment celui du Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé, qui lui a témoigné sa confiance. Marié et père de famille, Togbuigan Adovi Aboua II exerce la profession d’entrepreneur. ATOP/YM/AO

items.title: ADP crisis deepens as spokesman disputes Sani’s suspension
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The leadership crisis rocking the Action Democratic Party (ADP) has deepened, with the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Dr Sani Dawop, disputing the reported suspension of its National Chairman, Yabagi Yusuf Sani. Dawop insisted that Sani remains the party’s duly elected National Chairman, describing allegations of forgery, financial impropriety and interference with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) candidate nomination portal against him as unsubstantiated. He said no constitutionally valid decision had been taken to remove or suspend Sani, whose mandate was renewed at the party’s National Convention held on May 29 and 30, 2026. Dawop was reacting to a statement by the National Secretary, Victor Fingesi, announcing Sani’s interim suspension over allegations of forgery of party documents and unauthorised interference with INEC’s candidate nomination portal. Fingesi had said the notification of the suspension was formally communicated to INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, in a letter signed by him. According to Fingesi, the motion for Sani’s interim suspension was moved by the National Legal Adviser, Richard Hwande, seconded by the National Youth Leader, Chinazam Ike, and approved by a majority of NWC members present. When contacted by Vanguard on Friday, Sani declined to comment, replying in a text message: “No Comments.” However, in a statement on Saturday, Dawop said the party’s national leadership rejected the account of the purported suspension and the attempt to present the allegations and proceedings as the settled institutional position of the ADP. Dispute over NWC meeting Clarifying the proceedings of the Emergency National Working Committee (NWC) meeting held on November 4, Dawop said the meeting dealt with disciplinary concerns involving Fingesi, rather than the National Chairman. He said the meeting considered Fingesi’s responses to previous queries, alleged acts of insubordination, refusal to comply with lawful directives and conduct said to be capable of undermining party unity and discipline. According to him, the meeting also considered alleged actions by Fingesi that were contrary to the principle of party supremacy. Dawop said that after deliberations and appeals for Fingesi to retract disputed statements and apologise, the National Special Duties Secretary and Acting Deputy National Secretary, Fatima Sani Muhammed, moved a motion seeking the exercise of the NWC’s emergency powers under Article 23.2(e) of the ADP Constitution 2026. He said the motion sought Fingesi’s interim suspension from the functions of National Secretary, the commencement of a disciplinary investigation and referral of the decision to the National Executive Committee (NEC) for ratification. Dawop added that Fingesi and Ike were among the NWC members present at the meeting, which he said had the required quorum. He maintained that the motion was seconded and passed, with the interim suspension of Fingesi taking effect from November 4. “The Party therefore maintains that the operative disciplinary decision arising from that meeting concerned Hon. Victor Fingesi, not the National Chairman,” he said. ADP explains Fingesi’s suspension On Fingesi’s status, Dawop said the NWC decision followed a series of formal queries and opportunities given to the National Secretary to explain his conduct. He said the party leadership was particularly concerned by Fingesi’s alleged refusal to retract statements challenged by the leadership or apologise, citing his interpretation of Article 43.1.6 of the party’s constitution. Dawop said no party officer, regardless of position, should disregard lawful party decisions or undermine constituted authority. He described the interim suspension as a protective and disciplinary measure pending investigation and consideration by the NEC, stressing that it did not amount to a final determination of guilt. Sani rejects allegations On the allegations against Sani, Dawop said claims of forgery, interference with INEC’s nomination portal and financial impropriety required credible evidence, proper investigation and fair hearing. He said the National Chairman rejected the allegations and challenged those making them to submit verifiable evidence to the appropriate investigative and judicial authorities. The spokesman said the party would not accept unsubstantiated allegations as a substitute for constitutional procedures or as justification for what he described as an unauthorised takeover of its leadership. He also cautioned against presenting consultations on Nigeria’s political future as evidence of anti-party activities without due consideration of the facts and applicable party rules. Portal, finances under scrutiny On alleged irregularities involving the party’s INEC nomination portal, Dawop said the national leadership had previously raised concerns about suspected unauthorised access and activities on the platform. He called for independent investigations, preservation of electronic records and cooperation with INEC and relevant security agencies. He, however, said the existence of such concerns did not, on its own, establish wrongdoing by Sani or any other individual. On the party’s finances, Dawop reiterated the leadership’s commitment to transparency, proper accounting and lawful management of party resources. He said any request for an audit should be handled through the appropriate constitutional organs and established financial procedures, adding that allegations of financial misconduct must be supported by identifiable transactions, records and evidence. The spokesman also warned against the use of the party’s name, official letterhead and communication channels to misrepresent decisions or create an impression of authority not lawfully established. He said communications purportedly issued on behalf of the NWC to INEC or other institutions must reflect decisions genuinely reached in accordance with the party’s constitution. Dawop said the party would take appropriate constitutional and legal steps to challenge any communication or action found to misrepresent its resolutions. He urged party members, candidates, state chapters and supporters to remain calm and focused on preparations for the 2027 general elections, despite the internal disagreements. The spokesman reiterated that, according to the party’s position, the November 4 NWC meeting resolved to suspend Fingesi from the functions of National Secretary pending disciplinary investigation and NEC ratification, not Sani as National Chairman. The post ADP crisis deepens as spokesman disputes Sani’s suspension appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Agou/Culture : La 3e édition de Kebo Novitikplo célébrée à Kebo-Apeyeyeme
items.description: Agou-Gadzépé, 8 nov. (ATOP) – Les fils et filles du canton d’Agou Kebo ont célébré, le samedi 7 novembre à Kebo-Apeyeyeme, la troisième édition de Kebo Novitikplo. La rencontre est placée sous le thème « Contribution des jeunes d’Agou Kebo au développement de leur canton : enjeux et défis liés à l’éducation à la vie sociale ». Elle vise à améliorer la qualité des relations et du dialogue entre les populations ainsi que le respect des autorités locales. Elle entend faciliter la participation des communautés et la gestion efficace des moyens humains, techniques, matériels et financiers en faveur du développement communautaire. L’initiative ambitionne également d’aider les jeunes à acquérir les connaissances et les compétences nécessaires à leur pleine participation au processus de développement. Cette édition a été marquée par des parades de hamacs, des chants et danses folkloriques. Un chèque symbolique a été remis au président du Comité villageois de développement (CVD) de Kebo-Apeyeyeme pour la réalisation de travaux de développement. Le témoin « Novitikplo » a également été transmis au village d’accueil. Le directeur régional du Tourisme, de la Culture et des Arts des Plateaux-Ouest, Monkli Kokou, a indiqué que Novitikplo permet de mobiliser les communautés autour d’activités culturelles véhiculant des messages positifs. Il a réaffirmé la disponibilité de sa direction à apporter un appui technique au recensement, à la documentation et à la promotion du patrimoine culturel matériel et immatériel du canton. Les autorités traditionnelles Parades des Hamacs Le vice-secrétaire du bureau exécutif, Joseph Mawussi Afemeku, a présenté le bilan des activités du comité Novitikplo et les perspectives. Il a rappelé qu’en décembre 2025, à la suite de la rencontre du 8 novembre de la même année à Kebo-Dogbadzi, le comité avait échangé avec le préfet d’Agou et le député-maire de la commune Agou 1 sur les décisions prises et les actions à mener. Celles-ci concernaient notamment la cohésion sociale, la gouvernance locale, l’éducation, l’accès à l’eau et le développement des infrastructures. Pour 2026-2027, le comité prévoit poursuivre les actions inscrites dans sa feuille de route, notamment le règlement des questions foncières et la délimitation des emprises des villages. M. Afemeku a également annoncé l’accélération des démarches pour la construction d’un lycée dans le canton et l’électrification de Kebo-Apeyeyeme. Le comité envisage aussi l’élaboration d’une charte de solidarité cantonale et la signature d’accords de partenariat. Le chef canton d’Agou Kebo, Togbui Gbadegbe IV, a souhaité que Novitikplo soit un cadre d’échanges entre les générations, où la tradition et la modernité se complètent. Il a appelé les fils et filles du canton à renouer avec les bonnes pratiques d’antan et à s’impliquer davantage dans le développement de leur localité. Il a également exhorté les jeunes à se respecter, à respecter les autres et surtout les autorités, pour le bien-être de tous. Novitikplo est une rencontre annuelle organisée à tour de rôle dans les huit villages du canton de Kebo. Le village qui accueille chaque édition est désigné par tirage au sort. Pour 2027, le choix est porté sur Kebo-Toé. ATOP/BSM/AO

items.title: One dies as truck overturns in Lagos midnight crash
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni One person has died after a fully loaded Mercedes-Benz six-tyre truck overturned around the TREM axis of Gbagada, inward Oshodi, Lagos State, in a midnight accident. The deceased, an elderly man whose identity had yet to be established, was reportedly thrown out of the truck after one of its front tyres burst, causing the driver to lose control of the vehicle. The truck, with registration number ABJ 37 AC, was conveying assorted consignments, including sealed bags and newly branded event chairs, when the incident occurred. According to reports, the vehicle was travelling at considerable speed when the tyre burst. In the ensuing struggle to stabilise the truck, the passenger seated in the front cabin was flung out and hit his head against a sharp object, resulting in his instant death. The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) said its Night Rescue Team, which was conducting surveillance along major traffic corridors, promptly mobilised to the scene and cordoned off the accident site. The operatives subsequently evacuated the deceased from the busy carriageway into an ambulance operated by the Lagos State Emergency Medical Services (LASEMS), to prevent further exposure to approaching motorists and avert another accident. The General Manager of LASTMA, Mr Olalekan Bakare-Oki, expressed condolences to the family of the deceased, describing the incident as a painful and avoidable loss that underscored the dangers of poor road safety practices. Bakare-Oki said the rescue and traffic management operations received support from personnel of the Pedro Police Division, who provided security, and officers of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, who assisted with emergency response. He explained that the overturned truck could not be immediately recovered because of the volume and nature of its cargo. Arrangements were therefore made to transfer the consignments into another empty truck before recovering the vehicle. The LASTMA boss condemned excessive speeding, warning that it reduces drivers’ reaction time, compromises vehicle stability and increases the severity of road crashes, particularly when unexpected mechanical failures occur. He said the consequences of the accident could have been less severe if the truck had been travelling at a controlled speed, despite the sudden tyre burst. Bakare-Oki urged heavy-duty vehicle operators, commercial transporters and other motorists to adopt responsible driving practices, conduct regular mechanical inspections and pay close attention to the condition of tyres, braking systems and other critical vehicle components before embarking on journeys. He also advised drivers to remain calm and apply appropriate vehicle-control techniques when confronted with sudden mechanical problems, warning that excessive speed could turn a manageable failure into a fatal incident. According to him, roadworthiness, speed moderation and compliance with traffic regulations remain essential to safe motoring, particularly for operators conveying heavy loads on densely populated urban roads. He reaffirmed LASTMA’s commitment to proactive traffic surveillance, prompt emergency response and collaboration with relevant agencies to protect lives and ensure safety on Lagos roads. items.title: Liverpool return to winning ways with 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace
items.description: Florian Wirtz bagged his first Premier League goal this season as Liverpool got back on track with a 3-1 win against lowly Crystal Palace on Sunday. Andoni Iraola’s side erased the bitter taste of successive losses to Arsenal and Fenerbahce with a comfortable victory at Selhurst Park. Alexis Mac Allister put Liverpool ahead late in the first half before Wirtz, whose last league goal came against the same opponents in April, doubled the Reds’ advantage nine minutes into the second half. Alexander Isak netted Liverpool’s third in the 89th minute before Eddie Nketiah scored a stoppage-time penalty for bottom of the table Palace. Liverpool are up to fourth place after their fourth away league win this season. It was a much-needed success for Iraola, who had started to hear some awkward questions about Liverpool’s inconsistent run in his first season in charge after arriving from Bournemouth to replace the sacked Arne Slot. Yeremy Pino went agonisingly close to opening the scoring for Palace in the 18th minute when he curled against the bar. Palace striker Jorgen Strand Larsen had the ball in the back of Alisson Becker’s net in the 33rd minute. But his celebrations were cut short by the offside flag and a subsequent VAR check. Mac Allister made Palace pay for those misses in the 40th minute, nodding home a Dominik Szoboszlai free-kick in clinical fashion. Wirtz increased Liverpool’s advantage in the 54th minute, guiding a low Bradley Barcola cross into the bottom corner. Palace had a huge chance with just under 15 minutes remaining when Pino was denied by Alisson, who then saved from Jefferson Lerma before Nketiah lashed over. Sweden striker Isak put the result beyond doubt in the 89th minute with a deflected close-range strike. Palace earned a penalty after Dario Osorio clashed heads with Milos Kerkez but Nketiah’s goal was no consolation for under-fire Eagles boss Pierre Sage.
