items.title: Police repel cattle rustlers, recover 39 cows in Kaduna
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Kaduna State Police Command has repelled an attack by suspected cattle rustlers and recovered 39 stolen cows in Illa Village, Igabi Local Government Area of the state. The incident occurred at about 4am on Friday, November 7, 2026, when armed men reportedly invaded the community and rustled cattle belonging to three Fulani herders. The police said a 25-year-old man, identified as Abubakar, sustained gunshot wounds to both legs during the attack. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Mansir Hassan, disclosed this in a statement, saying the Divisional Police Officer, Rigachikun Division, received a distress call from one Alhaji Yahaya Abubakar of Illa Village at about 5am. Following the report, a combined team of police operatives, led by the Officer-in-Charge of Amana Outpost, alongside local vigilantes and community members, mobilised and pursued the fleeing suspects into the bush. According to the statement, the team engaged the rustlers in a gun duel, forcing them to abandon the stolen cattle and escape with suspected gunshot injuries. The police said eight rounds of ammunition were expended during the exchange of fire. The injured victim was subsequently taken to Shika Teaching Hospital for treatment, where he was said to be responding to medical attention. The 39 recovered cows have since been handed over to their owners. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, Muhammad Rabiu, commended the operatives and members of the community for their collaboration in foiling the attack. He assured residents that the command would sustain its efforts to combat cattle rustling and other criminal activities across the state. The post Police repel cattle rustlers, recover 39 cows in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Anambra begins reconstruction of failed roads ahead of Christmas
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Contractors handling major road projects in Anambra State have returned to site to reconstruct failed sections of the roads following a directive by the state government ahead of the forthcoming Christmas season. The development followed concerns over the failure of some portions of the roads, including sections that are yet to be officially commissioned. The affected projects include the Amawbia-Agulu-Ekwulobia-Uga dual carriageway, the Agulu-Nnewi dual carriageway and other major roads across the state. The Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Okey Ezeobi, had attributed the failures to extreme rainfall and flash flooding rather than the use of substandard construction materials. He, however, directed the contractors to undertake major reconstruction of the affected sections instead of carrying out temporary, spot repairs, in line with Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s emphasis on quality infrastructure delivery. Barely 12 hours after the directive, the contractors reportedly mobilised to their respective sites, with reconstruction work commencing across the state. At the Amawbia end of the dual carriageway, asphalt on one lane had been completely removed, while sand-filling work was ongoing. Similar activities were observed at the Neni section of the Agulu-Nnewi road and along the Nnewi-Ozubulu-Okija dual carriageway. During a visit to some of the project sites at the weekend, officials of the Ministry of Works were seen monitoring the progress of the reconstruction. Ezeobi had earlier dismissed allegations that the road failures resulted from poor construction, insisting that the contractors engaged by the state government were reputable companies capable of undertaking corrective work. “Because of the quality of these contractors, they are able to return to site to effect reconstruction whenever there is any failure and they do this at no cost to the state. “If we had given the contract to small companies, they won’t come back to address the failures. We took time to select all the contractors working for us,” he said. The commissioner attributed the affected portions to the impact of natural disasters, recalling that the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) had earlier issued warnings about possible flooding during the year. He explained that roads located in flood-prone areas were particularly vulnerable, citing sections of the Amawbia-Ekwulobia dual carriageway where swamps and underground water movements had contributed to the damage. “Roads along flood-prone areas in the state are adversely affected. For instance, the Amawbia-Ekwulobia dual carriageway is erosion-prone as there are swamps in some areas and the water there is always struggling to come up. “So in the affected places, we will remove the asphalt and do cement-based stabilisation to help suppress further underground water coming up to destroy it,” he said. Ezeobi assured that the affected roads would undergo reconstruction and quality checks before being certified for public use. He added that the government would announce the official opening of the roads after the contractors had completed the work and the projects had been certified. The post Anambra begins reconstruction of failed roads ahead of Christmas appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bauchi police arrest two suspected armed robbers, recover motorcycle
items.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested two suspected armed robbers and recovered a stolen motorcycle and other valuables following a machete attack on two residents of the state. The suspects, alongside a third accomplice who is still at large, allegedly attacked a 26-year-old man at his residence in the Rafin Makaranta area of Bauchi metropolis in the early hours of November 6, 2026, inflicting machete injuries on his head. The attackers, reportedly armed with machetes, also dispossessed the victim and his friend, a resident of Makera area, of a motorcycle, two mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, power banks, an MP3 player, perfume and N45,000 cash. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement issued on Sunday in Bauchi. Habib said operatives attached to the C Division responded to the incident and launched a manhunt for the perpetrators, leading to the arrest of two suspects on November 7. He identified the suspects as Uzairu Rabiu, alias Gwano, of Zawiyya area, Bauchi, and Hafizu Abdullahi, alias Tora, of Gubi village, Bauchi. According to him, the operatives recovered a stolen Haojue motorcycle, two mobile phones and a Bluetooth device from the suspects. The police spokesman added that the injured victim was receiving treatment at the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (ATBUTH), Bauchi, and his condition was steadily improving. He said efforts were ongoing to apprehend the third suspect and recover the remaining stolen items. Habib added that the arrested suspects would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, commended the operatives for their swift response and urged residents to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information to the police. He warned criminal elements to desist from violent activities, assuring residents that the command would sustain its operations to tackle armed robbery and other criminal activities across the state. items.title: 7è édition de Togo Fashion Awards : Des acteurs de la mode et de la beauté distingués
items.description: Lomé, 8 nov. (ATOP) – Les professionnels de la mode et de la beauté ont été distingués le samedi 7 novembre à Lomé, à l’occasion de la 7ᵉ édition de Togo Fashion Awards. La cérémonie a été organisée par l’agence de communication et d’événementiel Simera Corporation. Elle a mobilisé des stylistes, mannequins, modèles photo, esthéticiennes, coiffeuses, maquilleurs, accessoiristes et photographes. Les créations présentées ont également permis au public d’apprécier la diversité des talents. Au total, 14 catégories ont été retenues pour distinguer les professionnels du secteur et saluer leur contribution au développement de la mode et de la beauté au Togo. Les distinctions ont notamment concerné le Jeune styliste de l’année, le Meilleur styliste de l’année, la Révélation mannequin de l’année, les Mannequins masculin et féminin de l’année, les Modèles photo masculin et féminin de l’année, ainsi que le Créateur de contenus de l’année. Les salons d’esthétique et de coiffure, les prothésistes ongulaires, les maquilleurs, les accessoiristes, les boutiques de prêt-à-porter et de streetwear, y compris les photographes ont également été à l’honneur. Des prix honorifiques ont, par ailleurs, été attribués à des personnalités engagés dans la promotion et la valorisation de la mode et la beauté au Togo. Cette édition a enregistré la participation de professionnels venus du Sénégal et de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC). Le modèle congolais Tyshawax a remporté le prix de la Meilleure styliste africaine de l’année. Le promoteur de l’événement, Torrès Amededjisso, a expliqué que Togo Fashion Awards vise à reconnaître le travail des professionnels et à donner davantage de visibilité aux talents togolais. « Chaque année, nous célébrons les acteurs de la mode et de la beauté pour faire briller davantage leurs talents. Nous voulons aussi encourager l’excellence, valoriser les professionnels et contribuer au rayonnement de la mode togolaise au-delà des frontières nationales », a-t-il déclaré. Le public a également participé à la soirée en désignant la plus belle tenue, dont le lauréat a reçu une récompense de 50 000 FCFA. ATOP/AO/AR

items.title: ‎Labour demands immediate start to new Minimum Wage talks
items.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ ‎ABUJA— THE Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) has accused the Federal Government of ignoring the statutory timetable for the next national minimum wage review, insisting that negotiations should already be under way rather than waiting until 2027. ‎ ‎NLC Acting General Secretary, Comrade Benson Upah, speaking to Vanguard in Abuja, said the current N70,000 minimum wage was agreed on July 28, 2024 and backdated to May 1, 2024, but argued that the backdating did not alter the three-year review cycle introduced by the 2024 amendment to the Minimum Wage Act. ‎ ‎“In our estimation, the negotiations ought to have been on the way, or ought to be on the way, because one, the economic realities have since wiped out the value of the ₦70,000, upon which the minimum wage was premised,” Upah said. ‎ ‎He said the 2023 amendment changed only two things: the wage figure, from ₦30,000 to ₦70,000, and the review cycle, from five years to three years, adding that neither change authorised government or labour to shift the commencement date of the three-year cycle at will. ‎ ‎“The principal act was not amended, and there was nothing in the amended items that states that the three yearly cycle can be abridged by either of the parties. ‎ ‎“It is clear that this thing runs on the three yearly cycle now. It is like the constitution says a governor shall hold office for four years, and the governor has to hold office for four years.” ‎ ‎Upah argued that, on the NLC’s reading of the law, the three-year period should be counted from the earlier wage cycle, meaning negotiations ought to have started in June. He said the NLC had already alerted government to that position. ‎ ‎He said: “But if you want to follow the government logic, which is actually an error, that because it took effect from May, that the three years will start from May, if you follow that logic, the negotiations ought to start in November, because the act talks about starting six months before the process. ‎ ‎“So, in our view, there is no reason to do tomorrow what can be done today.” ‎ ‎The NLC scribe said the process of reviewing the minimum wage was lengthy and required hearings, consultations, a cost-of-living assessment and engagement with social partners. ‎ ‎According to him: “It is important for us to start early. Why must we run on a deficit calendar when we knew full well that this thing was going to start on a so-so date? It speaks to our state of unpreparedness.” ‎ ‎His position comes amid an ongoing dispute over when the next review should begin. The Federal Government has maintained that the current N70,000 wage is due for review on June 1, 2027, while organised labour has demanded immediate preparations for a new negotiation. ‎ ‎Asked about suggestions by some labour leaders that the next minimum wage would commence in August 2027, Upah dismissed the claim sharply, saying: “Whichever union leader that made that comment clearly spoke out of ignorance, and acted in error. ‎ “Whichever index you use in assessing this matter, whether by way of fact or by way of law, we are on the right side of history.” ‎ ‎Pressed on whether the government was right to rely on the Minimum Wage Act’s stipulated duration, Upah said the NLC’s interpretation was the correct one. ‎ ‎He said the 2024 amendment did not annul or alter the entire Minimum Wage Act, but only amended the wage figure and review cycle. ‎ ‎He said: “So the presumption is that the cycle is a three yearly cycle, and it is not a cycle that either party can vary whimsically or at their whims and caprices, no. ‎ ‎“It is a statutory issue. It is already stated there, so I cannot wake up and say, okay, this is when the three years will start. Neither can government now say this is when the three years can start.” ‎ ‎He hinted that the NLC was prepared to seek judicial interpretation if necessary. ‎“On this matter, let me tell you, we can go to court for an interpretation.” ‎ The post ‎Labour demands immediate start to new Minimum Wage talks appeared first on Vanguard News .

Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 to escape Premier League bottom
items.description: Sunderland hauled themselves off the bottom of the Premier League as Enzo Le Fee’s penalty earned a huge 1-0 win over Chelsea for embattled boss Regis Le Bris. The Frenchman was under pressure after a dismal 2-0 home defeat to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League on Thursday put his position in doubt ahead of an international break. Sunderland, though, bounced back for a huge three points thanks to two controversial penalty decisions. Chelsea were furious that Cole Palmer was not awarded a spot-kick for a foul by Luke O’Nien moments before the only goal of the game. A VAR review deemed the contact made was outside the area and therefore could not be overturned. Sunderland were awarded a penalty at the other end 10 minutes before half-time. The visitors were again aggrieved that Levi Colwill was adjudged to have fouled Brian Brobbey as both players grappled in their attempt to reach the ball. Le Fee dispatched the resulting spot-kick past Mike Penders and Sunderland held on for just a second league win of the season. Chelsea missed the presence of Joao Pedro up front as Palmer and Morgan Rogers were kept in check by the home side. A fourth defeat in 10 league games under Xabi Alonso leaves the Blues in fifth, two points outside the top four. The post Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 to escape Premier League bottom appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tiflet : mobilisation contre l'impunité et les atteintes à la mémoire des symboles de la résistance
items.description: Plusieurs organisations de gauche et de défense des droits humains ont organisé, dimanche à Tiflet, un rassemblement pour dénoncer les propos attribués au conseiller parlementaire, Mahmoud Archane et les attaques visant la mémoire de l’ancien résistant Mohamed Bensaïd Aït Idder. Les manifestants ont également réclamé la poursuite du processus de vérité et de justice concernant les violations des droits humains commises durant les années de plomb. Une mobilisation à forte portée mémorielle et politique s’est tenue dimanche à Tiflet. À l’appel de la section locale de l’Association marocaine des droits humains (AMDH), plusieurs organisations politiques et associatives de gauche se sont rassemblées pour dénoncer ce qu’elles considèrent comme des tentatives de réhabilitation des responsables des violations graves des droits humains commises durant les années de plomb. Les manifestants ont notamment réclamé que les personnes impliquées dans ces violations soient soumises à des procédures de reddition des comptes, rejetant leur accès à des postes de responsabilité et les propos qu’ils jugent offensants à l’égard des figures de la résistance et du militantisme marocains. La mobilisation fait suite à une intervention controversée du conseiller Mahmoud Archane, fondateur du Mouvement démocratique et social (MDS) et ancien commissaire de police, lors de la discussion du programme gouvernemental devant la Chambre des conseillers. Il avait alors qualifié ses détracteurs de « cinquième colonne ». Les protestataires ont également dénoncé les propos attribués à Mustapha Boumahdi, membre du même parti, qui a qualifié le résistant et militant de gauche Mohamed Bensaïd Aït Idder de « traître » et d ' »agent ». © Hicham Msellek Layam Reddition des comptes Prenant part au rassemblement, la présidente de l’AMDH, Souad Brahma, a présenté cette mobilisation comme une prise de position collective contre toute tentative de retour des personnes mises en cause dans les violations des années de plomb à des fonctions de responsabilité. Dans une déclaration à Hespress, elle a dénoncé ce qu’elle considère comme une provocation envers les victimes de cette période, évoquant les souffrances des anciens détenus politiques et les atteintes subies par les familles des victimes. Elle a notamment appelé à ce que les responsabilités soient établies et que toute la vérité sur les violations commises soit rendue publique. « Il n’y aura ni apaisement ni résignation sans que les auteurs soient soumis à un examen de leurs responsabilités », a-t-elle affirmé, réitérant la volonté de l’association de poursuivre son action jusqu’à ce que les victimes obtiennent réparation. Interrogée sur les démarches engagées pour donner suite aux recommandations de l’Instance équité et réconciliation (IER), Souad Brahma a indiqué que l’association continuait de porter cette revendication à travers différentes initiatives sur le terrain. Elle a également plaidé pour la mise en place d’un mécanisme crédible permettant d’assurer l’application de ces recommandations, ainsi que pour l’organisation d’une deuxième conférence nationale consacrée à l’examen des violations et à la question de la reddition des comptes. © Hicham Msellek Layam La mémoire de Mohamed Ben Saïd Aït Idder au cœur des protestations Pour Jamal El Asri, secrétaire général du Parti socialiste unifié (PSU), le rassemblement de Tiflet entend également dénoncer les tentatives de déformation de l’histoire nationale et les atteintes à la mémoire des figures de la résistance marocaine. Il a notamment critiqué le fait que les propos contestés aient été tenus sans réaction de l'autorité présente lors des sessions communales, alors que celle-ci est notamment chargée de veiller au respect de la légalité et des dispositions constitutionnelles. Évoquant Mohamed Bensaïd Aït Idder, le responsable politique a rappelé son parcours de résistant et de militant, ainsi que la reconnaissance officielle dont il a bénéficié à travers une distinction royale. Il a également souligné la diversité des personnalités politiques et sociales présentes à ses funérailles. De son côté, la militante des droits humains Khadija Ryadi a estimé que la mobilisation ne se limitait pas à une réaction aux déclarations récentes. Elle a appelé à poursuivre le travail de dénonciation des violations passées, rappelant que les actes de torture et les enlèvements constituent des crimes qui ne doivent pas être frappés par la prescription. Elle a également élargi les revendications des manifestants à la situation actuelle des libertés publiques, appelant à garantir le droit à l’expression, à l’organisation et à l’opinion, ainsi qu'au respect des engagements internationaux du Maroc en matière de droits humains. © Hicham Msellek Layam L’héritage des années de plomb toujours au centre du débat La mobilisation a également été soutenue par des élus locaux. Azz El Harb Halimi, conseiller communal à Tiflet représentant la Fédération de la gauche démocratique (FGD), a expliqué que la manifestation visait en premier lieu les déclarations de Mahmoud Archane devant la Chambre des conseillers, notamment sa référence à la « cinquième colonne ». Il a cité parmi les victimes des années de plomb Driss Benzekri, originaire de Tiflet, et dénoncé ce qu’il considère comme une atteinte à la mémoire des personnes qui ont milité pour la liberté, la dignité et la justice sociale. L’élu a par ailleurs affirmé avoir lui-même été visé par des propos de Mustapha Boumahdi, vice-président du conseil communal de Tiflet, au sujet de Mohamed Bensaïd Aït Idder. Il a expliqué que sa réaction s’inscrivait dans la volonté de préserver la mémoire nationale et d’éviter que les drames du passé ne se reproduisent. © Hicham Msellek Layam The post Tiflet : mobilisation contre l'impunité et les atteintes à la mémoire des symboles de la résistance appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Lagos arrests dismissed operative for impersonation, extortion
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Taskforce has arrested a former operative of the agency, identified as 36-year-old Adeyemo Olalekan, for allegedly impersonating enforcement personnel, unlawfully seizing commercial motorcycles and extorting their operators across the state. The arrest came as the agency disclosed that another suspect, earlier arrested over similar offences, had been remanded at the Kirikiri Correctional Centre. Preliminary investigations reportedly revealed that Olalekan was a former staff member of the agency who was dismissed several years ago over alleged theft-related misconduct. Despite his dismissal, he allegedly continued to pose as a Taskforce operative, conducting illegal arrests and demanding money from victims in exchange for the release of their motorcycles. The suspect was arrested on Sunday following a tip-off received through the agency’s official hotlines. One of his alleged victims, who became suspicious of his activities, contacted the Taskforce and subsequently discovered that he had been dismissed from the agency. Speaking on the arrest, the Chairman of the Lagos State Taskforce, CSP Adetayo Akerele, said operatives responded to the complaint and apprehended the suspect while he was allegedly attempting to extort two commercial motorcycle operators whose motorcycles he had unlawfully seized. Akerele said the suspect had reportedly evaded arrest on several previous occasions before he was eventually apprehended. He added that the agency had been tracking individuals involved in similar fraudulent activities following repeated complaints from members of the public. The chairman described the impostors as criminal elements who exploit the identity and authority of the Taskforce to unlawfully apprehend motorcycle operators and demand money for the release of their motorcycles. According to the agency, the suspect allegedly targeted brand-new Bajaj motorcycles and motorcycles with engine capacities below 200cc, particularly those operating on highways and other restricted routes. He reportedly confessed that he disguised himself as a genuine passenger, approached unsuspecting motorcycle operators and paid their fares before identifying himself as an enforcement officer. He would then allegedly threaten to have their motorcycles crushed unless they paid him money. The suspect has been arraigned before a court on three counts bordering on impersonation, extortion and conduct likely to cause a breach of public peace. He reportedly pleaded guilty to all three charges. The case was adjourned until December 16, 2026, for facts and sentencing, while the defendant was remanded at the Kirikiri Correctional Centre. Akerele reiterated the agency’s determination to rid Lagos of individuals exploiting its identity to perpetrate criminal activities, warning that dismissed personnel and others involved in impersonation would be made to face the law. In a related development, the agency said Yahaya Salami, also known as Adams, who was arrested in October over alleged impersonation and extortion, appeared in court again. Salami pleaded not guilty to the charges, and the case was adjourned until December 9, 2026. He was remanded at the Kirikiri Correctional Centre pending the fulfilment of his bail conditions. Taskforce impounds 128 motorcycles Meanwhile, the Taskforce said it had impounded 128 commercial motorcycles during a fresh enforcement operation against their activities on highways and other restricted routes. The operation covered Festac First Gate, Apple Junction, Trade Fair, Apapa, Coconut Bus Stop and Mile 2 areas of the state. Akerele urged residents to remain vigilant and report suspicious activities by anyone claiming to be a Taskforce operative through the agency’s official feedback channels. “There is no more room for official recklessness or criminality in Lagos. “Anyone found impersonating our personnel or using the name of the agency to extort members of the public will be tracked down and made to face the full weight of the law,” he said. The post Lagos arrests dismissed operative for impersonation, extortion appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Aide à l’Ukraine : l’UE face au gouffre de la dette, tandis que le budget 2028-2034 patine
items.description: La dette totale de l'Union europeenne liee a l'aide apportee a l'Ukraine pourrait depasser les 200 milliards d'euros si l'UE prend de nouveaux engagements, rapporte Die Welt am Sonntag . Selon les estimations du journal, fondees sur les donnees de la Commission europeenne, Bruxelles devrait verser a Kiev plus de 40 milliards d'euros sous forme de prets conjoints, en plus des 166 milliards d'euros deja alloues. Selon les plans actuels, sur les 70 milliards d'euros de financement supplementaire demandes par l'Ukraine, l'UE est prete a en couvrir 46. Une partie de cette somme proviendrait des interets generes par les avoirs russes geles, mais ces versements ne representeraient que quelques milliards d'euros par an. Die Welt am Sonntag a souligne que les actifs eux-memes ne seraient pas utilises et que de nouvelles obligations de dette conjointes constituaient donc l'alternative la plus probable. L'Union europeenne prevoit le versement d'une nouvelle tranche a Kiev, alors que la concertation sur le budget pour la periode 2028-2034 se heurte a des difficultes. Les negociations sur cette question sont deja dans l'impasse en raison de divergences entre les pays exigeant une reduction des depenses et ceux qui insistent pour maintenir les subventions a l'agriculture et au developpement regional. Robert Fico, Premier ministre slovaque, a averti qu'il serait tres difficile pour l'UE de s'accorder sur le nouveau budget de l'Union pour les sept prochaines annees. Le prochain sommet informel des dirigeants de l'UE se tiendra le 13 novembre a Dublin, avec pour theme officiel l'intelligence artificielle. Toutefois, les principaux points de discorde devraient porter sur les questions budgetaires et le financement de Kiev. Le precedent sommet de l'Union, qui s'est tenu les 15 et 16 octobre, n'a pas permis de resoudre ces divergences. Un sommet extraordinaire consacre a cette question est prevu les 26 et 27 novembre a Bruxelles. Si aucun accord n'est trouve, les discussions se poursuivront lors de la reunion du Conseil europeen des 17 et 18 decembre. Moscou condamne le soutien financier et militaire apporte a l'Ukraine par les pays occidentaux, estimant qu'il ne fait que prolonger le conflit. En avril dernier, le secretaire du Conseil de securite russe, Sergueï Choïgou, a critique la decision de l'Union europeenne d'accorder un pret de 90 milliards d'euros a l'Ukraine. Selon lui, l'octroi de ces fonds constitue un pas de plus vers la perte de souverainete des pays europeens.

items.title: Aïssata Sia Camara revient sur sa rencontre avec le président Doumbouya : « J’étais comme au paradis »
items.description: Cette infirmière devenue ouvrière sur les chantiers de Koloma, Aïssata Sia Camara avait fait parler d'elle après la diffusion de ses images aux côtés du président guinéen Mamadi Doumbouya. Depuis cette rencontre, elle aurait été reçue au palais Mohammed V et aurait bénéficié de plusieurs avantages, dont les clés d'une maison à Yattaya, dans la haute banlieue de Conakry. Sur le chantier de Koloma, selon ses dires, elle ne voulait pas manquer l'occasion de s'approcher du président Mamadi Doumbouya. Alors que les personnes présentes étaient retenues à distance, elle raconte avoir réussi à se frayer un chemin pour aller saluer les autorités. Une démarche qui l'a finalement conduite à se retrouver aux côtés du chef de l'État. Lors de son passage à la télévision parlementaire,dame Aissata Sia,a raconté, dans un témoignage marqué par son admiration pour le président, comment cette rencontre s'est déroulée. « On était retenus et on était nombreux, mais moi, je me suis échappée. Je suis allée vers eux. J'ai d'abord salué le Général Balla Samoura, après je suis allée vers le Général Amara Camara, je l'ai salué et je lui ai dit : « Je suis ta sœur, puisque moi aussi je suis Camara » », explique-t-elle. Après avoir salué les deux responsables, elle se retrouve au moment où le président demande aux personnes présentes de venir prendre une photo. Mais, par respect pour celui qu'elle considère comme son président, elle préfère d'abord garder ses distances. « Moi, je me suis arrêtée juste en dessous de lui, puisque c'est mon Président et je dois le respecter. Mais je ne m'y attendais pas. J'avais déjà formulé des prières auprès de Dieu. Quand je me suis arrêtée, il m'a dit : « N'aie pas peur, approche-toi ici ». Il m'a fait monter près de lui », raconte-t-elle. Cette invitation du chef de l'État n'est pas le seul souvenir qu'elle garde de cette journée. Elle affirme avoir également entendu Dansa Kourouma, qui l'avait envoyée travailler sur le chantier, intervenir auprès du président pour lui rappeler ses qualités professionnelles. « Quand il m'a fait monter, j'ai entendu mon Président Dansa Kourouma dire : « C'est elle, je l'ai envoyée sur le site ici ». Il a rajouté : « Elle vaut plus qu'un homme, partout où on la met, elle est bonne là-bas ». » Face au président, Aïssata Sia Camara dit avoir été submergée par ses émotions. Elle raconte même lui avoir murmuré son affection à l'oreille. « J'ai murmuré à son oreille : « Je vous aime, je vous aime ». Il a répondu : « Oui ». Je voyais mes sentiments et mes émotions augmenter, et il fallait que je prouve que je l'aime. Je voulais même mordre sa main, je ne voulais même pas le laisser », confie-t-elle. Dans son récit, elle n'oublie pas non plus Dansa Kourouma, qu'elle considère comme son bienfaiteur. Elle explique avoir également retenu la main de ce dernier au cours de la scène, refusant de minimiser le rôle qu'il a joué dans son parcours. « Quand il m'a tirée, moi aussi j'ai tenu la main de mon bienfaiteur, Dansa Kourouma. Il ne faut pas sous-estimer le bienfaiteur, quoi qu'il en soit. C'est grâce à lui qu'on est là aujourd'hui », souligne-t-elle. Au moment de quitter le président, elle dit avoir eu du mal à se détacher de lui. Elle explique que cette émotion lui a également rappelé le départ de Mamadi Doumbouya des États-Unis, un souvenir qui, selon elle, avait laissé en elle beaucoup de frustration. Mais cette rencontre sur le chantier de Koloma n'a pas été la dernière. Interrogée par le journaliste sur un deuxième face-à-face avec le chef de l'État, Aïssata Sia Camara confirme avoir été reçue au palais Mohamed V. « Oui, je l'ai vu chez lui, dans le grand salon à M5 », répond-elle. À la question de savoir comment elle avait vécu ces retrouvailles, elle ne cache pas une nouvelle fois son émotion : « J'étais comme au paradis, je n'ai même pas voulu laisser ses mains. Il est gentil, il aime les gens, donc nous aussi, aidons-le. » Au cours de cette même émission, elle est également revenue sur son engagement pendant la campagne présidentielle. Elle affirme avoir accompagné Dansa Kourouma dans ses déplacements pour soutenir Mamadi Doumbouya. Elle raconte notamment une scène au cours de laquelle elle avait exprimé son soutien au candidat à travers un chant et un geste auquel d'autres personnes présentes avaient fini par prendre part. « Quand je suis partie pour les campagnes, j'ai chanté pour Doumbouya en disant : « Doumbouya, qu'est-ce que je peux faire pour toi ? Me coucher par terre et me rouler ». Je me suis couchée par terre et tout le monde m'a suivie, hommes comme femmes, chacun s'est roulé par terre », raconte-t-elle. Pour Aïssata Sia Camara, cet engagement était une manière de témoigner son attachement au président. Elle estime que ses prières ont été exaucées et appelle les Guinéens, toutes catégories confondues, à soutenir le chef de l'État. « Ce que je dirais aux Guinéens, aux femmes, aux jeunes, aux vieux, à tous réunis : soutenons tous le Général Mamadi Doumbouya. Il a bon cœur, il a pitié, il est tolérant, il aime les gens sans penser à l'ethnie », déclare-t-elle. Elle invite également les citoyens à accompagner les personnes choisies par le président pour exercer des responsabilités. « Ceux qu'il a choisis pour travailler, il faut les aider. Là où il t'a mis, il faut suivre, c'est Dieu qui paie l'homme », conclut-elle. Christine Finda Kamano L’article Aïssata Sia Camara revient sur sa rencontre avec le président Doumbouya : « J'étais comme au paradis » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: 2027: Nigeria is boiling, Tinubu must douse tension now — Turaki
items.description: …Accuses APC of using violence, courts to weaken opposition …Cites declining confidence in INEC, judiciary …Jerry Gana urges President to act as father of the nation, not partisan politician By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Interim National Working Committee, Kabiru Tanimu Turaki, SAN, has urged President Bola Tinubu to urgently address rising political tension and violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that Nigeria could descend into crisis if the situation is allowed to deteriorate. Turaki said attacks on opposition politicians, intimidation of voters and declining public confidence in electoral institutions were threatening the credibility of the elections, insisting that no political ambition was worth the survival of the country. He spoke at a press conference in Abuja, where he presented a statement titled, The Country Is Boiling; Can We Reduce the Temperature? The PDP’s Interim National Working Committee, accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of shrinking the political space, encouraging attacks on opposition parties and using the judiciary to undermine political competition. Drawing parallels with the First and Second Republics, Turaki warned that the suppression of opposition parties and manipulation of electoral processes had contributed to political instability and democratic collapse in Nigeria’s past. Citing Yiaga Africa’s third National Voting Intentions Survey, released on October 7, 2026, he said 84 per cent of Nigerians were willing to vote, but 61 per cent feared violence could keep them away from polling stations. Only 34 per cent expressed confidence in the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), while 63 per cent had little or no confidence in the judiciary’s ability to resolve electoral disputes fairly. The PDP chairman cited alleged attacks on supporters of Peter Obi, the ADC presidential campaign of Atiku Abubakar and activist Omoyele Sowore, including incidents in Delta, Sokoto and Ekiti states. He accused APC-linked operatives of being behind the incidents, while also alleging that opposition parties were being weakened through politically motivated court cases and voter intimidation. He further accused some public officials of threatening voters with displacement if they failed to support the APC, warning that such actions could undermine Nigerians’ freedom to choose their leaders. Comparing the political rhetoric of successive presidents, Turaki recalled former President Goodluck Jonathan’s declaration ahead of the 2015 election that his ambition was not worth the blood of any Nigerian. He contrasted this with former President Muhammadu Buhari’s controversial pre-election warning that the country would be soaked in blood if he was prevented from winning, and Tinubu’s reported remarks that elections were not a tea party and victory must be grabbed, snatched and run with. He said: “Nigeria is bigger than anybody and the ambition of any individual. We must appreciate that this country must survive for you to become whatever you want to become. “Whether you want to be a president, you want to be a governor, you want to be a member of National Assembly or an ordinary councillor in your ward, you must have a country first.” Turaki warned that electoral victory secured through intimidation and violence could become a pyrrhic one if the winner failed to earn the confidence of Nigerians. “You may win at the end of the day, but it may end up being a pyrrhic victory. You win, but you have not won the soul of the people,” he said. He called on Tinubu to publicly condemn political violence and ensure the investigation and prosecution of those implicated in attacks on opposition politicians and supporters. The PDP also demanded that security agencies publish an election security plan, governments stop denying opposition parties access to public campaign facilities, INEC address alleged discrepancies in the voters’ register, and the judiciary dispense justice without executive interference. Former Minister of Information, Professor Jerry Gana, who also addressed the press conference, backed Turaki’s appeal, urging Tinubu to act as President and father of the nation rather than as a partisan politician. Gana said the President had a responsibility to protect the peace, security and stability of Nigeria, even where doing so might run contrary to his party’s political interests. He said: “Anything that will bring this nation to peace, you will not be part of it. Even if it will benefit the APC, as father of the nation, you should arise and arrest it.” Gana added that the PDP was choosing restraint despite its capacity to respond to political provocation, insisting that violence would only hurt the country. “If you wanted to go and say you want to promote violence and we wanted to answer by violence, it can be done. But we don’t want to do that, because it’s not good for Nigeria. It’s not healthy for Nigeria,” the ex-minister stressed. The post 2027: Nigeria is boiling, Tinubu must douse tension now — Turaki appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Foreign Affairs Ministry refers 2 interdicted officers to police over illegal passport scheme
items.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has referred two of its officers to the Ghana Police Service for further investigations and possible prosecution over their alleged involvement in an illegal Service Passport issuance scheme. The officers are the Acting Director of Passports, Mahama Yahaya Amantana, and a junior Foreign Service Officer, Alhassan Sumani, who have both been interdicted pending investigations into the matter. According to the Ministry, Mr Sumani, who was recruited into the Foreign Service on November 29, 2024, was named in all the petitions as the alleged chief architect of the scheme. He is also accused of operating as a “goro boy” in 2023 before joining the Foreign Service. In a statement issued on Sunday, November 8, 2026, the Ministry said the decision to refer the two officers to the police followed preliminary findings into allegations that individuals who did not qualify for Service Passports obtained them through illegal payments to a syndicate. The investigation was triggered by two petitions received on October 8, 2026, with the Foreign Affairs Minister, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, subsequently directing the formation of a committee on October 13 to examine the allegations. The Ministry further disclosed that retired Ambassador Mohammed Habib Idris, who was Director of Passports during the period in 2023 when some of the irregularities occurred, would also be investigated by the security services and sanctioned if found culpable. It said it was committed to ensuring that all persons implicated in the alleged scheme are held accountable, adding that the investigation would be guided by transparency, impartiality and fairness.

items.title: FG secures $200m World Bank funding to boost fish production
items.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has secured a $200 million World Bank-backed financing commitment to boost fish production across the country through state governments, as part of efforts to reduce import dependence and strengthen Nigeria’s aquaculture industry. The funding, to be made available to state governments as concessional loans, is expected to support investments in fisheries and aquaculture, expand production capacity and create opportunities for private-sector participation. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, disclosed this at a high-level executive training on the Aquaculture Investment Guide organised by the ministry in collaboration with the World Bank Group in Abuja. Oyetola, who was represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Marine and Blue Economy, Prof. Busayo Fakinlede, said the financing would help states unlock their fisheries potential and develop commercially viable aquaculture projects. The minister, in a statement issued by his Special Adviser, Bolaji Akinola, said the Federal Government was prioritising collaboration with state governments, investors and development partners to position Nigeria as a fish-sufficient nation. He said expanding domestic fish production had become imperative to address the widening gap between local supply and consumption. According to him, the involvement of state governments is critical to achieving the country’s fish production targets. “Fish is a pillar of food security, household nutrition and rural livelihoods. No nation can call itself food secure while it imports most of the fish it eats. Our ambition is to produce more, import less and, in time, become a net exporter. That ambition can be achieved only when every state plays its part,” he said. Under the proposed framework, states are expected to identify priority aquaculture value chains, assess investment opportunities, develop bankable projects and commit to measurable contributions towards national fish production. Oyetola said the executive training was designed to equip state policymakers and technical officials with the expertise to translate investment opportunities into viable projects. He said the programme would focus on business models, risk management, environmental safeguards and public-private partnerships. The minister commended the World Bank Group for its support for Nigeria’s marine and blue economy development, particularly in analytical studies, capacity building and the development of the Aquaculture Investment Guide. He also disclosed plans to convene a stakeholders’ roundtable after the training to strengthen engagement with state governments, investors and development partners and establish implementation arrangements for the financing initiative. Meanwhile, Fakinlede said the ministry had increased national fish production from 1.1 million tonnes to 1.4 million tonnes through interventions aimed at strengthening the sector. He identified the inauguration of the Technical Committee on Accelerating Fish Production in August 2026 and the digitisation of fish import licensing as some of the measures introduced by the ministry. He further disclosed that Nigeria had secured shrimp-export certification following compliance with Turtle Excluder Device requirements. According to him, the ministry has also developed the Fish City and Fish Terminal investment portfolio to attract private-sector capital into the fisheries and aquaculture industry. items.title: NAF redeploys senior officers, appoints new commanders
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has announced a major redeployment of senior officers, appointing new Air Officers Commanding (AOCs), Principal Staff Officers (PSOs) and commanders across its operational commands, training institutions and strategic establishments. The exercise, approved by the Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, on November 7, 2026, takes effect from November 2026. Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed this in a statement, saying the appointments cover the NAF Headquarters, operational commands, Defence Headquarters, training institutions and other strategic establishments. He said the exercise was designed to align leadership competencies and professional experience with the Service’s evolving operational and institutional priorities. At NAF Headquarters, AVM AK Ademuwagun has been appointed Chief of Transformation and Innovation; AVM IV Ajiboye, Superintendent of Standards and Evaluation; AVM PN Amadi, Chief of Air Intelligence; AVM NN Ananaba, Chief of Operations; AVM AH Bakari, Air Provost Marshal; AVM EE Efiom, Chief of Training; and AVM MS Ibrahim, Chairman, Air Expo and International Liaison. Other appointments at the headquarters include AVM AG Kehinde as Chief of Civil-Military Relations; AVM MA Sulaiman as Chief of Communications and Information Systems; AVM S Peters as Coordinator, Project Implementation Team; and AVM AJ Laoye as Chief of Aircraft Engineering. AVM AY Dari becomes General Manager, Nigerian Air Force Investment Limited Group of Companies, while AVM NS Okoro has been appointed Director-General, AFRDI. New operational commanders At the operational command level, AVM NI Ilo has been appointed Air Officer Commanding, Tactical Air Command; AVM BR Mamman, AOC, Mobility Command; AVM OS Ogunsina, AOC, Logistics Command; AVM MN Onyebashi, AOC, Special Operations Command; and AVM FCS Nwakara, AOC, Ground Training Command. To strengthen operational command structures, AVM JI Ukeh has been appointed Commander, Nigerian Air Defence Corps. Other command appointments include AVM OA Abu as Chief of Staff, Mobility Command; AVM I Subi as Chief of Staff, Special Operations Command; AVM NB Folaji as Chief of Staff, Tactical Air Command; AVM F Ekpah as Chief of Staff, Ground Training Command; AVM ES Odekina as Chief of Staff, Logistics Command; and AVM M Umar as Chief of Staff, Air Training Command. AVM GI Jibia has also been appointed Deputy Force Commander, Operation HADIN KAI. Defence Headquarters, strategic appointments At the strategic defence level, AVM UK Abdullahi has been appointed Director of Defence Operations at Defence Headquarters (DHQ), while AVM EOE Ebiowe moves to the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) as Deputy Coordinator, National Intelligence. Other appointments include AVM DDG Pwajok as Director of Technical Services, Defence Intelligence Agency; AVM I Sani as Deputy Chief of Defence Intelligence; AVM AA Shinkafi as Director of Liaison, DHQ; AVM AO Shogbamu as Director of Military Strategy; AVM RK Olanrewaju as Director of Search and Rescue; AVM J Usman as Director of Special Duties; AVM JJ Ijudigal as Director of Sports; AVM ZA Usman as Director of Cyber Operations; AVM EK Gabkwet as Director of Civil-Military Relations; and AVM GAA Bello as Director of Joint Warfare Doctrine. At the Defence Space Administration, AVM AA Suleh has been appointed Deputy Chief, while AVM OA Oyename becomes Director of Earth Observation and AVM SS Lazarus, Director of Launch Vehicles and Space Operations. AVM OT Salami has been posted to the Defence Space Command Centre as Deputy Chief, while AVM AI Hanidu becomes Director of Integrated Air Power Studies at the Air Power Centre of Excellence (APCOE). Other APCOE appointments include AVM OF Akinboyewa as Deputy Director-General and AVM MM Omar as Director, Museum/Hall of Fame. AVM DO Dickson has also been appointed General Manager, Operations, Defence Health Care Limited. Training institutions, other appointments In major institutional appointments, AVM PB Philips has been appointed Commandant, Armed Forces Command and Staff College, while AVM MC Ekwueme becomes Commandant, Armed Forces Resettlement Centre. Other appointments include AVM AO Akinbunwa as Commandant, Air Force War College; AVM A Idris, Commandant, Air Warfare Doctrine Centre; AVM JA Ekwuribe, Commandant, Regiment Training Centre; AVM OC Ubadike, Commandant, Air Force Institute of Technology; AVM AI Sambo, Commandant, Nigerian Air Force College of Logistics and Management; and AVM M Yusuf, Deputy Commandant, Nigerian Defence Academy. Additional professional military education appointments include AVM SA Eyoma as Deputy Commandant, Air Force Institute of Technology; AVM FO Ankeli as Commandant, Air Traffic Services Training Centre; and AVM U Ariahu as Deputy Commandant, Nigerian Air Force College of Logistics and Management. At NAF Headquarters, AVM AK Famuyiwa has been appointed Director of Coordination and Cooperation; AVM AK Bello, Director of Armament; AVM YA Katabiya, Director of Logistics; AVM EO Ashiegbu, Director of Policy; AVM GA Mbaka, Director of Aircraft Engineering; AVM AL Dakwat, Director of Research and Development; AVM SO Eyekosi, Director of Plans; and AVM AG Akinyimika, Director of Personnel Management. Meanwhile, AVM CE Akubue has been appointed Managing Director, Aircraft Engineering and Technical Services Limited, while AVM CE Akpa becomes Commander, Headquarters NAF Camp. The statement said the strategic realignment reflected the NAF’s commitment to leadership renewal, stronger institutional accountability and enhanced operational effectiveness. According to Ejodame, the CAS expressed confidence that the professional competence and experience of the newly appointed officers would advance his Command Philosophy and strengthen the Service’s capacity to deliver decisive airpower effects in support of joint operations and national security objectives. All affected officers are expected to assume their new appointments and complete the necessary handover and takeover formalities on or before November 13, 2026. items.title: Navy uncovers 68,175 litres of suspected stolen crude in Rivers
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has uncovered approximately 68,175 litres of suspected stolen crude oil at illegal storage and refining sites in Ogbogolo Community, Ahoada West Local Government Area of Rivers State. The discoveries were made during two separate operations conducted on October 24 and November 7, 2026, by personnel of the Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Soroh under Operation Delta Sentinel. The Director of Information, Nigerian Navy, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the operations followed credible intelligence on illegal petroleum storage and refining activities within the Orashi Forest and adjoining areas. According to him, the naval team, during the October 24 operation, discovered two crude oil storage sites containing four dugout pits, 29 sacks and a 25-litre keg, with an estimated 8,675 litres of suspected crude oil. He said a subsequent operation on November 7 led to the discovery of two illegal refining sites comprising two large and 36 small dugout pits, alongside other storage facilities containing an estimated 59,500 litres of suspected stolen crude oil. Folorunsho said the discovered petroleum products and associated items were handled in accordance with established procedures. He explained that the operations underscored the Navy’s sustained intelligence-led efforts under Operation Delta Sentinel to dismantle illegal petroleum storage and refining infrastructure, disrupt crude oil theft networks and deny criminal elements access to the nation’s natural resources. He added that the Navy would maintain operational pressure in identified areas of criminal activity to support the protection of critical oil and gas infrastructure and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. The Navy, he said, remained committed to sustaining the operations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders to combat crude oil theft, disrupt illegal refining activities and protect the nation’s maritime and economic interests. items.title: Aliko Dangote to join President Mahama at Invest Ghana Summit 2026
items.description: Africa’s foremost industrialist and business leader, Aliko Dangote, will join President John Dramani Mahama to open the Invest Ghana Summit (IGS) 2026, Ghana’s premier international investment and business forum, scheduled for 16th and 17th November 2026 at the Kempinski Hotel, Gold Coast City, Accra. The Summit is expected to draw investors, multinational corporations, policymakers and business leaders from around the world, reinforcing Ghana’s standing as one of Africa’s most attractive destinations for investment and regional expansion. Convened by the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), with support from the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry; Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA); Bank of Ghana (BoG); Ghana Free Zones Authority (GFZA); National African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Coordination Office; and the 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development Programme (24H+), and in partnership with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Finance, the President-led Summit will connect international capital with investment-ready opportunities across manufacturing, agribusiness, infrastructure, energy, logistics, healthcare, mining, tourism, digital technology and the creative economy. Held under the theme “Investing in Ghana’s New Economy: Building a Productive Economy that Creates Value and Competes Globally”, the Summit will showcase Ghana’s renewed investment proposition and accelerate partnerships that support the country’s economic transformation agenda. This includes the government-led US$10 billion investment programme (2026–2030) to shift the country from economic stabilisation to production-led growth, with major funding for agriculture, manufacturing, energy, mining value‑addition, tourism and other productive sectors, as well as the recently enacted GIPA Act, which strengthens the investment facilitation framework and enhances investor support services. Africa’s Industrial Future A key highlight of the Summit will be an exclusive fireside conversation with Aliko Dangote, during which he will share lessons from building one of Africa’s largest industrial conglomerates and discuss opportunities to scale investment, strengthen regional value chains, and advance Africa’s industrial development. The session will be followed by a keynote address from President John Dramani Mahama, who will outline Ghana’s economic transformation agenda and the country’s vision for investment-led growth, industrialisation and export expansion. According to Simon Madjie, Chief Executive Officer of GIPA, Mr Dangote’s participation sends a strong signal to the international investment community of Ghana’s growing appeal as a destination for large-scale industrial investment. “Mr Dangote’s presence at the Invest Ghana Summit is a powerful endorsement of Ghana’s economic potential and investment outlook. As one of Africa’s most respected industrial leaders, he will enrich discussions on industrialisation, regional value chains and private-sector-led growth, while inspiring investors and entrepreneurs seeking to build globally competitive businesses from Africa.” Another major attraction for investors will be the Investor Facilitation Hub, which will bring together 19 public institutions under one roof to provide real-time support for business registration, taxation, permits, immigration services, incentives, environmental approvals, and other regulatory requirements. The summit will also host an AfCFTA Investment Breakfast to explore opportunities arising from Africa’s single market, with discussions covering industrialisation, regional value chains, investment facilitation, and how businesses can leverage Ghana’s position as host of the AfCFTA Secretariat to expand across the continent. Investment Opportunities A distinguishing feature of the Summit is its focus on investment execution. Participants will gain direct access to a pipeline of investment-ready projects spanning strategic sectors of the economy. Highlighted projects include the Eastern Railway Line Development Project, the Accra-Tema Motorway Expansion Project, the Volo-Battor Agro-Industrial Park, the Volta Lake Transport System, the Legon Pharmaceutical Innovation Park, the Tamale Air Cargo and Logistics Hub, and the Buipe Solar and Battery Storage Project. The Summit will also showcase regional investment opportunities through the GIPA Investment Opportunities Mapping Project (IOMP), including cocoa processing, cashew processing, rice farming, cassava starch production, tomato processing, livestock production, and agricultural logistics infrastructure in the Bono, Bono East, and Ahafo Regions, Others include the US$1.46 billion Buipe Solar and Storage Project in the Savannah Region, which will power regional inland ports, logistics hubs, and agro-industrial parks through a dedicated commercial vehicle (24H Parks Energy PLC); the Green Forestry and Climate Investment Corridor project spanning six regions, including Western North, Ashanti, Bono East, Eastern, Savannah and Oti, to promote commercial forestry and carbon market projects, among others; and investment prospects in the development of safari lodges, wellness resorts, conference facilities, and cultural heritage destinations aimed at attracting both domestic and international travellers. In addition, participants will engage in curated business-to-business and business-to-government meetings, investment deal rooms, and sector-focused panel discussions on regional investment, pharmaceuticals and the industrial value chain; digital economy, technology and services; energy and green industrial growth; mining, minerals and the downstream value chain; infrastructure, transport and logistics; creative economy, tourism and diaspora connections for investment and economic growth; fintech and the future of financial services in Ghana; and networking sessions with regulators, project promoters and financiers. Driving Economic Impact Highlighting the event’s broader significance, Mr Madjie said the Summit is expected to stimulate business expansion, create jobs, drive industrialisation, deepen technology transfer, and unlock new export opportunities. “By connecting investors directly with bankable projects and decision-makers, we are creating a platform that turns investor interest into tangible economic outcomes for Ghana,” he added. About the Invest Ghana Summit and GIPA The Invest Ghana Summit is Ghana’s flagship President-led investment promotion platform, bringing together investors, policymakers, business executives, development partners, and entrepreneurs to explore investment opportunities and foster strategic partnerships for economic growth. The Ghana Investment Promotion Authority is the primary government agency responsible for encouraging, regulating, and facilitating investment in and outside Ghana. It operates under the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority Act, 2026 (Act 1173), which replaced the older Ghana Investment Promotion Centre (GIPC) Act of 2013.

items.description: By Benjamin Njoku Nigerian music icon, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, thrilled music fans in Mbeya, Tanzania, with an energetic performance at the Bongo Flava@30 anniversary festival. 2Baba was among the headline performers at the festival, held on Saturday, November 7, 2026, at Eden Highlands Hotel in Mbeya, as Tanzania’s music industry marked 30 years of Bongo Flava. The Nigerian singer’s appearance added an international flavour to the celebration, which brought together some of Tanzania’s established music stars to reflect on the growth and influence of the country’s popular music genre. His performance reportedly drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, further demonstrating his appeal to music lovers beyond Nigeria. Other artistes who performed at the festival included Bongo Flava pioneers and established acts such as Mr Blue, Afande Sele, Kalapina, Juma Nature, Gangwe Mob and Chidi Benz. The festival was part of activities marking the 30-year journey of Bongo Flava, a genre that has evolved from a local Tanzanian sound into an influential force in contemporary African music. 2Baba’s participation also highlighted the growing cultural ties between Nigeria and Tanzania, particularly through music and entertainment. Widely regarded as one of Africa’s influential musicians, 2Baba has built a career spanning several decades, with hit songs that have earned him a broad following across the continent. His appearance in Mbeya further underscored the reach of Nigerian music and the growing cross-border influence of African artistes. The post 2Baba thrills fans at Bongo Flava@30 festival appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026-Triple saut : Sokhna Fatoumata Touré bat son record personnel
items.description: La Sénégalaise Sokhna Fatoumata Touré a disputé la finale du triple saut aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse de Dakar 2026 ce 08 novembre 2026. Elle a terminé huitième et dernière, mais son concours reste une réussite personnelle. Au meilleur moment, devant son public, elle a franchi 11 m 56 et amélioré son record personnel. Le classement ne reflète donc pas la valeur de son saut. Pour une athlète de cet âge, battre son record dans une finale d'une telle ampleur est un signe de progression. Sans médaille à la clé, Sokhna Fatoumata Touré repart avec une expérience précieuse et une marque qui confirme son potentiel. Avec le soutien du public dakarois, cette finale pourrait bien être le premier jalon d'un parcours à suivre. O.B.N

items.title: Mise en service de la station intégrée de dessalement de l’eau de mer à Jebha
items.description: La Société régionale multiservices (SRM) de Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceima a procédé, cette fin de semaine, à la mise en service de la station intégrée de dessalement de l’eau de mer à Jebha, dans la province de Chefchaouen, dans le cadre de la célébration du 51e anniversaire de la Glorieuse Marche Verte et du premier anniversaire de la Fête de l’Unité. La cérémonie de mise en service s’est déroulée en présence du gouverneur de la province de Chefchaouen, Zakaria Hachlaf, de représentants des autorités locales, d’élus et de partenaires institutionnels, dans le cadre des efforts visant à renforcer la sécurité hydrique et à diversifier les sources d’approvisionnement en eau potable. Mobilisant un investissement global d’environ 13 millions de dirhams (MDH), financé par le ministère de l’Intérieur, le projet a été réalisé sous la maîtrise d’ouvrage déléguée de la SRM. Il s’inscrit dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des Hautes Orientations Royales visant à assurer la sécurité hydrique du Royaume, à mobiliser les ressources disponibles et à accélérer la réalisation de projets destinés à faire face au stress hydrique et aux effets du changement climatique. Cette nouvelle infrastructure permettra d'améliorer les conditions d'approvisionnement des populations de Jebha et d'Amter, tout en renforçant l'offre hydrique à l'échelle locale, a déclaré a la presse le directeur général adjoint chargé de l’exploitation au sein de la SRM-TTA, Younes Hajjaj. La station, a-t-il ajouté, permettra de produire quotidiennement quelque 864 mètres cubes d'eau dessalée, soit 10 litres par seconde, au bénéfice d'environ 14.500 personnes, notamment dans les communes de Jebha et d'Amtar, contribuant ainsi à améliorer les conditions d’approvisionnement en eau potable dans la région. Le projet comprend notamment l'installation d'une station compacte de dessalement utilisant la technologie de l'osmose inverse, l'équipement d'un forage d'un débit de 24,3 litres par seconde, ainsi que la réalisation de conduites destinées au transport de l'eau brute et de l'eau traitée. Il porte également sur la mise en place des ouvrages annexes et le raccordement de la station au réseau électrique à travers un transformateur dédié. © MAP Le processus de traitement repose sur plusieurs étapes, notamment la filtration et le prétraitement, l'osmose inverse, la reminéralisation et la désinfection finale, afin de garantir une eau répondant aux normes de qualité requises pour la consommation humaine. La mise en service de cette infrastructure permettra de renforcer les capacités locales de production d'eau potable et de diversifier les sources d'approvisionnement dans la province de Chefchaouen. Elle devrait également contribuer à réduire les risques de perturbation de la distribution et à améliorer la fiabilité du service, particulièrement durant les périodes de forte demande. The post Mise en service de la station intégrée de dessalement de l’eau de mer à Jebha appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Kamel Daoud : sa femme s’exprime sur leur divorce et l’affaire « Houris »
items.description: Nouvelle sortie publique de Aïcha Dahdouh , l’épouse de Kamel Daoud poursuivie avec lui par Saada Arbane qui les accuse de violation de sa vie privée dans le roman “Houris”. Après un communiqué transmis à l’AFP fin octobre, Aïcha Dahdouh s’est exprimée dans un entretien diffusé par le site algérien Casbah Tribune ce dimanche 8 novembre. D’emblée, elle confirme son divorce avec l’écrivain et chroniqueur du magazine Le Point. “Mon souhait était de me présenter à mon procès, le 13 octobre. Je n’ai pas pu le faire, en raison de notre situation familiale : nous sommes engagés dans une procédure de divorce, et j’ai le devoir d’anticiper l’impératif de la garde des enfants”, dit-elle. Cette affaire a pesé, mais elle n’est pas la seule raison du divorce, révèle la femme qui met en avant ses profondes divergences avec l’écrivain sur de nombreuses questions, comme l’islam, l’Algerie ou la Palestine. Aïcha Dahdouh, épouse de Kamel Daoud : “Je suis innocente” Psychiatre ayant suivi Saada Arbane qui a survécu toute jeune à un attentat terroriste en Algérie dans les années 1990, Aïcha Dahdouh est accusée d’avoir raconté les détails du calvaire de la victime à son mari qui en a fait un roman. “Houris” a été primé en 2024 du prix Goncourt en France. Ce qu'elle nie catégoriquement. “Non, jamais. Il n’y a jamais eu aucune porosité entre ma vie professionnelle et ma vie privée. C’est un principe fondamental, que je respecte comme tous les praticiens”, assure-t-elle. “Je suis innocente. Je n’ai jamais trahi le secret médical, et je n’ai jamais sorti ni remis aucun dossier médical”, insiste la psychiatre. Affaire Houris : ce qu'il s'est passé, selon la femme de Kamel Daoud Elle reconnaît néanmoins avoir eu des échanges avec madame Arbane dans “des cadres différents, notamment amicaux”, expliquant que leurs enfants réciproques étaient “amis”. “C’est dans ce cadre qu’elle voyait mon mari, avec qui elle a échangé à plusieurs reprises, en ma présence ou non”, dit-elle, ajoutant qu’elle a noté des “similitudes” entre le personnage d’Aube de Houris et madame Arbane et qu'elle a signalé cela aux éditeurs avant la parution du livre, “par devoir de protection”. Aicha Dahdouh révèle que la mère adoptive de Saada Arbane avait “souhaité, de son vivant, que l’histoire de sa fille soit racontée par Kamel Daoud”. Selon elle, Mme Arbane était au courant de la volonté de sa mère et a “accédé à sa demande”. “En 2022, une rencontre a donc eu lieu chez nous, un soir de Ramadan. J’ai fait les présentations, puis je suis allée m’occuper des enfants. Je n’ai pas assisté à leur échange. À l’issue de cette rencontre, l’un comme l’autre m’ont dit qu’ils s’étaient mis d’accord sur le projet du livre”, raconte-t-elle. Sauf que la concernée a retiré plus tard son consentement et le message a été transmis à Kamel Daoud oralement, “comme cela se fait entre des familles qui se connaissent”. “Les écrits et les positions de Kamel Daoud n’engagent que lui” Aïcha Dahdouh s’est aussi démarquée des positions controversées de Kamel Daoud. “Je sais aussi que le retentissement des positions de Kamel Daoud en Algérie est très lourd, et que cela m’a beaucoup impactée. Mais ses positions ne sont pas les miennes”. dit-elle. “Aujourd’hui, je parle par devoir de vérité. Je ne peux pas accepter que sa voix efface la mienne. Je parle aussi pour mon métier. La psychiatrie, en Algérie, revient de loin. La psychiatrie coloniale servait à justifier la domination. Frantz Fanon a rompu avec elle et rendu au patient sa dignité”, explique la psychiatre. “Les écrits, les positions et les prises de parole de Kamel Daoud n’engagent que lui, tranche-t-elle. Je peux dire ce que je suis et ce que je choisis. Je suis profondément attachée à ma patrie, l’Algérie. Je suis musulmane, de naissance, de culture et de confession. Je refuse toute violence commise au nom d’une religion, comme je refuse la stigmatisation de toute religion et de ceux qui la pratiquent.” Assurant qu’elle refuse que l’on “hiérarchise les souffrances”, Aïcha Dahdouh indique que, sur ce qui se passe à Gaza, elle voit, en médecin, “l’ampleur d’une catastrophe humanitaire, dont les blessures dureront des générations”. “Je respecte sa liberté. Mais respecter sa liberté ne m’oblige pas à renoncer à la mienne. J’ai besoin d’être alignée avec mes valeurs”, assène-t-elle à propos des positions de Kamel Daoud. L’article Kamel Daoud : sa femme s’exprime sur leur divorce et l’affaire « Houris » est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Israël : Gadi Eisenkot officiellement chargé de former le prochain gouvernement
items.description: Le président israélien a officiellement remis dimanche à Gadi Eisenkot, chef du principal bloc d’opposition au premier ministre sortant Benyamin Nétanyahou, le mandat de former le prochain gouvernement, tout en relevant qu’Israël faisait face à une « nouvelle réalité politique » après les élections américaines. « L’État d’Israël a besoin d’un gouvernement stable […] Eisenkot, j’attends de vous que vous mettiez tout en œuvre pour former un gouvernement qui servira aussi bien ceux qui ont voté pour vous que ceux qui ne l’ont pas fait » , a déclaré Isaac Herzog lors d’une cérémonie à la résidence présidentielle à Jérusalem. « Nous devons faire avancer les processus diplomatiques dans la région après la guerre, mettre en œuvre le plan en 20 points du président Trump [pour la bande de Gaza, NDLR] » et « faire face à une nouvelle réalité politique » aux États-Unis, a-t-il ajouté. Gadi Eisenkot s’est dit dimanche ouvert à la participation du parti Likoud du premier ministre sortant, et de la formation d’un de ses alliés d’extrême droite à un gouvernement de coalition qu’il dirigerait. « Si les membres du Likoud et du Parti sioniste religieux [du ministre des Finances sortant Bezalel Smotrich] estiment sincèrement que l’heure est à l’unité […] je ne vois aucune raison pour laquelle ils ne soutiendraient pas un gouvernement dirigé par moi et fondé sur les principes que j’ai présentés », a-t-il dit. items.title: Kaduna-Kano rail line ready for December 3 inauguration — APC
items.description: …Kano-Katsina-Maradi project reaches 70% completion The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council has said the Kaduna-Kano Standard Gauge Railway will be inaugurated on December 3, 2026, as the Federal Government accelerates the completion of major railway projects in Northern Nigeria. The council also disclosed that the 203-kilometre Kaduna-Zaria-Kano railway project had reached approximately 90 per cent completion, while the 400-kilometre Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway project had attained 70 per cent completion. In a statement on Sunday, signed by its spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said the projects demonstrated President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to expanding railway infrastructure, improving regional connectivity and facilitating the movement of passengers and goods. It said the Kano-Katsina-Maradi project was barely five per cent complete when Tinubu assumed office in 2023, while the Kaduna-Kano railway was less than 30 per cent complete. According to the statement, the Kaduna-Kano railway, an extension of the existing Abuja-Kaduna standard gauge line, will establish a continuous rail connection between Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano, linking major commercial centres in Northern Nigeria. The council said the two projects were recently inspected on the directive of the President by a Federal Government delegation led by the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Engr. Funso Adebiyi. It said Adebiyi expressed satisfaction with the quality of construction work, particularly the railway alignment, drainage infrastructure, embankment protection, stone pitching and soil stabilisation. The inspection also included a train test run from Jaji in Kaduna State to Kano to assess the completed track infrastructure and passenger comfort. The statement added that Tinubu had directed the immediate resolution of outstanding land acquisition and compensation issues within Kaduna metropolis to facilitate the completion of the railway corridor from Abuja to Kano. It further disclosed that the completed 190-kilometre Jaji-Kano section of the Kaduna-Kano railway and the 250-kilometre Dawanu-Kano-Kazaure-Daura-Katsina section of the Kano-Maradi project would be inaugurated on December 3, 2026. When fully operational, the Kaduna-Kano railway is expected to improve passenger transportation, facilitate commercial activities and provide an alternative to road travel along one of Northern Nigeria’s busiest commercial corridors. Similarly, the Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway is expected to strengthen cross-border transportation and trade between Nigeria and neighbouring Niger Republic. The council reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to completing ongoing infrastructure projects across the country in line with its development agenda. The post Kaduna-Kano rail line ready for December 3 inauguration — APC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ibom Deep Sea Port: NDC questions Tinubu’s fresh approval
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has questioned the latest approval of the proposed Ibom Deep Sea Port by President Bola Tinubu, recalling that the project had earlier received approval under former President Muhammadu Buhari in December 2020. The opposition party accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of making repeated promises on the project without delivering on previous commitments, asking how many times the Federal Government would approve the same port. In a statement on Sunday, signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the NDC recalled that the Federal Executive Council (FEC), under Buhari, had on December 16, 2020, approved the implementation of the first phase of the $4.6 billion Ibom Deep Sea Port project. It said the approval named Bollore/Power China as the preferred bidder and was intended to pave the way for the commencement of construction. The statement, titled, “APC’s Endless Lies and Deceit: How Many Times Will APC Approve Ibom Deep Sea Port?”, followed Tinubu’s announcement of approval for the proposed port during his visit to Akwa Ibom State on November 6, 2026. The NDC also recalled that Tinubu, as the APC presidential candidate, had promised to build the port during the party’s campaign rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on January 30, 2023. Quoting the President’s campaign remarks, the party said he had told supporters: “We will do mechanised farming. We will export food from Akwa Ibom. We will build your seaport.” It, however, accused the APC of failing to fulfil the promise, arguing that the latest announcement amounted to a fresh commitment on a project that had already received federal approval. “In a brazen display of ignorance of statecraft and the elevation of grand deceit as a campaign strategy, President Tinubu, as APC presidential candidate, first promised the port during his 2023 campaign,” the party said. The NDC described the latest announcement as another promise that might not be fulfilled, urging Nigerians to hold the ruling party accountable for its previous commitments. Drawing a comparison with the Federal Government’s electricity supply promises, the opposition party said residents of Akwa Ibom were still waiting for the proposed deep sea port despite the earlier approval. It also urged Nigerians to reject the APC in future elections, declaring that a new Nigeria was possible under the NDC. The post Ibom Deep Sea Port: NDC questions Tinubu’s fresh approval appeared first on Vanguard News .
